modules.title: The q-binomial theorem, fibre sums, and Schur polynomials in the coefficients
modules.note:
The q-binomial theorem is proved as a sum over the subspaces of a vector space over a field with `q`
elements. There is a lemma on grouping a finite sum by the fibres of a map. Schur polynomials are
defined without division, as integer polynomials in the coefficients of a monic polynomial; `s_l(r)`
denotes the Schur polynomial with exponent tuple `l`, evaluated at a tuple of roots `r`. Three
algebraic facts serve to extract values of Schur polynomials from vanishing linear forms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.q_binomial_submodule`: the sum of `New.heckePolyCoeff X U` over the subspaces `U` of `W` is
  `New.SiegelWeil.qPochhammer q (dim W) X`.
* `New.Variety.genericSchur`, `New.Variety.rootCoeffEval`: the Schur polynomial in the coefficients,
  and evaluation at the coefficients of the monic polynomial with a given multiset of roots.
* `New.Variety.rootCoeffEval_genericSchur_mul_det`: the value times the Vandermonde determinant is
  `det (r i ^ l j)`.
* `New.Variety.sum_lagrange_smul_rootCoeffEval`: for distinct elements r₁, …, r_a of a field,
  summing s_l(r₁, …, X rᵢ, …) against the Lagrange factors ∏_{k ≠ i} (X rᵢ − r_k)/(rᵢ − r_k)
  gives s_l(r)·∑ⱼ X^(l j).
* `New.Variety.map_prod_rootCoeffEval_eq_zero`: a linear form that kills the families
  j ↦ ∏_{i, σ} ∏_{t ∈ x(j, σ)} (1 − c(i, σ)(α) t) for all α, with the c(i, σ) algebraically
  independent, kills the products over σ of polynomials of bounded degree in the coefficients of
  ∏_{t ∈ x(j, σ)} (X − t).
modules.literature:
Known results: the q-binomial theorem, counted over the subspaces of a finite vector space, and the
bialternant formula for Schur polynomials.

modules.title: Open subgroups, a tube lemma, and procyclic images of ℓ-adic characters
modules.note:
This file collects auxiliary facts from topology and algebra. It characterises congruence modulo a
principal ideal `(a)` by divisibility of the difference by `a`.

## Main definitions and results

* `IsCompact.eventually_forall_mem`: a form of the tube lemma for a jointly continuous map of two
  variables, with the continuity hypothesis discharged by `fun_prop` by default.
* `New.Selmer.exists_procyclic_generator`: a continuous character of a compact group with values in
  1 + 4ℤ_ℓ has procyclic image.
* `MonoidHom.IsGeneratorModKer`: an element generates a topological group modulo the kernel of a
  homomorphism; `New.Selmer.exists_isGeneratorModKer` gives one for such a character of a profinite
  group.

modules.title: Absolutely integrally closed rings and their stability properties; Frobenius powers
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
* `New.Variety.frobPow`: the ring endomorphism `x ↦ x ^ p ^ f`, for a prime `p` with `p = 0` in
  the ring.
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed`: every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root (the
  ring need not be a domain).
* The property passes to subrings that are integrally closed in the ring
  (`New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.of_isIntegrallyClosedIn`), to quotients
  (`New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.of_surjective`) and to localisations
  (`New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.of_isLocalization`). For a field it means algebraically
  closed: algebraically closed fields have it by an instance, and
  `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.isAlgClosed` gives the converse.
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.exists_root_map_eq`,
  `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed.mem_range_of_isIntegralElem`: for `f : A →+* B` from an
  absolutely integrally closed ring into a domain, roots in `B` of monic polynomials over `A` lift
  to roots in `A`, so integral elements lie in the image.

modules.title: Adic completeness: p-adic tools, extension by continuity, topological bases
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file collects tools on adic completeness over a commutative ring. It covers normed fields over
`ℚ_[p]`, divisibility by powers of an element `π`, maps of adic completions, monoid actions by ring
endomorphisms, extension of linear maps by adic continuity, and topological bases. In the results on
topological bases, `I` is an ideal of `S`, often `I = (p, z)`, and `M` is an `S`-module. For
`c : New.Lift.AdicBasis I M`, the `c.b i` are its vectors and the `c.coord i` its coordinate forms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.shiftDiff`: the operator `(x_j) ↦ (x_j - π x_{j+1})` on sequences. By
  `New.isPrecomplete_of_shiftDiff_surjective`, if it is onto for `π = x` and for `π = y`, then
  `(x, y)`-adic Cauchy sequences converge.
* `New.Adic.ringHom_ext_of_approx`: two ring maps `F`, `G` from `A` to a `p`-adically separated ring
  are equal if every element of `A` is congruent, modulo each power of `p`, to an element on which
  they agree.
* `New.adicMap`: a ring map that carries `I` into `J` induces a map of adic completions.
* `New.exists_adic_extension`: a linear map `g` into an `I`-adically complete module extends along a
  map `β` with dense image, if `β f ∈ I ^ (n + n) • ⊤` implies `g f ∈ I ^ n • ⊤` for all `n`.
* `New.Lift.exists_adicBasis`: an `I`-adic topological basis of `M` over `S` exists when
  `I = (p, z)` is maximal, `S` is `I`-adically complete, `p` is zero or injective on `M`, and `z` is
  injective on `M / p M`. It may be taken to contain given vectors independent modulo `I M`.
* `New.free_finite_of_rank_le`: over a ring `S` that is complete for a maximal ideal `(p, z)`, a
  separated module of finite rank on which `p, z` behave as a regular sequence (or `p = 0` and `z`
  is regular) is finite and free. The proof uses the topological basis of
  `New.Lift.exists_adicBasis`.

Notions of this file:
* `New.Lift.AdicBasis`: a topological basis of `M` over `S` for the `I`-adic topology: vectors `b i`
  whose finite combinations are dense, with linear forms `coord i` on `M` that read off the
  coefficients of a finite combination.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.PadicComparison.Completion` for sources.

modules.title: Power series with prime power exponents, congruences and convergent sums
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file studies power series of the form `∑_{i ∈ I} z ^ p ^ i` and congruences between power
series modulo a constant `π`, with the facts on continuity and convergent sums that are needed to
work with such congruences.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.primePowerSeries`: the series `∑_{i ∈ I} z ^ p ^ i`.
* `New.primePowerSeries_even_pow`: in characteristic `p` the `p`-th power of `∑_{i even} z ^ p ^ i`
  is `∑_{i odd} z ^ p ^ i`.
* `New.exists_eq_pow_add_pow_of_coeff_mul_ne_zero`: a product of two series `∑_{i ∈ I} z ^ p ^ i`
  has only terms of the degrees `p ^ i + p ^ j`.
* `New.dvd_sum_pow_sub_sum`: for a prime `p` the `p ^ j`-th powers are additive modulo a divisor of
  `p`.
* `New.continuous_subst_of_constantCoeff_eq_zero`, `New.continuous_pderiv`: substitution of finitely
  many series without constant term and differentiation are continuous.
* `New.C_dvd_of_hasSum`: over the valuation ring of `ℂ_[p]` a convergent sum of power series
  divisible by `π` is divisible by `π`.

Power series carry the topology of coefficientwise convergence.
modules.literature:
Known result: elementary facts on power series in characteristic `p`.

Known result: elementary facts on formal power series with the topology of coefficientwise
convergence. Source: Bourbaki, Algebra II, Chapter IV.

modules.title: Higman's criterion, dévissage and multiplicative functions on finite modules (Cartan map)
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Tools that reduce a statement about finite `l`-power-torsion discrete `G`-modules to simple cases;
they serve the inequality of local duality (`Lib.ClassField.LocalDuality.DualityInequality`) and the
cocycle counts of `Lib.ClassField.GreenbergWiles.CocycleCounts`.

* `New.DiscreteModule.IsHigmanProjective`: Higman's criterion, some additive `τ` has `∑ g τ g⁻¹ = 1`
  over `G ⧸ Q`.
* `New.DiscreteModule.FiniteKilledFixedInj`: the module is finite, killed by `n` and fixed by `Q`,
  and `ρ z - m` is injective on it.
* `New.DiscreteModule.diagonalPermModule`: the functions `Y → A` with the diagonal action of `G`.
* `New.DiscreteModule.devissage_induction`: dévissage to modules killed by `l` and fixed by a normal
  subgroup `P`.
* `New.DiscreteModule.exists_open_sylow`: an open `P ≥ U` of index prime to `l` whose elements have
  an `l`-power power in `U`.
* `New.DiscreteModule.IsMultiplicative.eq_one_of_eq_one_on_isHigmanProjective`: on the finite
  modules killed by `l` and fixed by `U` with `ρ z - 1` injective, `z` central modulo `U`, a
  function with values in `ℚ≥0` that is multiplicative in short exact sequences is `1` as soon as it
  is `1` on the modules with Higman's property.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DiscreteModule R G`: an `R`-module with the discrete topology and a continuous `R`-linear
  action `ρ` of the topological group `G`.
modules.literature:
Known result: The Cartan map has finite cokernel. It is stated for multiplicative functions with
nonnegative rational values on finite modules killed by a prime on which one element, central modulo
the level, fixes no nonzero vector, with projectivity read as Higman's property. It is proved using
functions on two parallel affine hyperplanes instead of Brauer characters or Artin induction.
Source: J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups (1977), Thm 35; for the route by
induction from cyclic subgroups in the local Euler characteristic formula, Milne, Arithmetic Duality
Theorems, I 2.10-2.12.

modules.title: Long exact sequences, four and five lemmas, and Ext with disjoint unions and products
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Long exact sequences of abelian groups are packaged as a structure, so that diagram chases, among
them the four and five lemmas, are proved once for all cohomology sequences. In the category
`New.Variety.AbFunctor C` of functors from `C` to abelian groups, with `New.Variety.H N F n`
denoting Ext^n(N, F), short exact sequences in either variable give long exact Ext sequences, and
comparison maps give morphisms between them.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.LongExactSeq`, `New.Variety.LongExactSeq.Hom`: the sequences and their morphisms.
* `New.Variety.LongExactSeq.Hom.four_lemma` (four lemma) and
  `New.Variety.LongExactSeq.Hom.five_lemma` (five lemma).
* `New.Variety.LongExactSeq.contravariant`, `New.Variety.LongExactSeq.covariant`: the long exact Ext
  sequences of a short exact sequence in the first and in the second variable;
  `New.Variety.Comparison.pull_hom_contravariant` and `New.Variety.Comparison.pull_hom_covariant`
  say that comparison maps give morphisms between them.
* `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_iff_subsingleton`: in a short exact sequence 0 → X₁ → X₂ → X₃ → 0, the
  map X₁ → X₂ is an equivalence for F iff the quotient X₃ has no cohomology with values in F.
* `New.Variety.H.sigma_bijective`: the cohomology `New.Variety.H (freeAb.obj Y) F n` of a disjoint
  union `Y = New.Variety.sigma X` of set-valued functors is the product of the cohomology groups of
  the `X i`, by pull-back (`New.Variety.H.map`) along the inclusions.
* `New.Variety.H.pi_bijective`: the map Ext^n(N, ∏ F_i) → ∏ Ext^n(N, F_i) is bijective, for the
  objectwise product `New.Variety.piAbFunctor`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv`: α: N' → N is an equivalence for F: the pull-back
  Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N',F) is bijective for every n; `New.Variety.AllBijective f` says that every
  map f n is bijective.

modules.title: Multivariate polynomials: cost of vanishing, homogenization, Nullstellensatz, Hensel
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file collects lemmas on polynomials in several variables and on algebras of finite type. They
cover commuting partial derivatives, generation by products of polynomials in two sets of variables,
the cost of monomials of polynomials that vanish to high order, and homogenization along a linear
form.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_le_weight_of_mem_vanishingIdeal_pow`: a nonzero polynomial that vanishes to order `d`
  at enough suitable points has a monomial of cost at least `d`.
* `New.exists_isHomogeneous_sub_one_dvd_sub` replaces a polynomial `P` of total degree at most `N`
  by a form `G`, homogeneous of degree `N`, congruent to `P` modulo `F - 1` for a given linear form
  `F`. So `G` and `P` have the same value at every point where `F` equals `1`
  (`New.exists_homogenization`); points are `R`-algebra maps `φ` out of the polynomial ring, with
  values in algebras in `Type`.
* `New.nullstellensatz_exists_le_ker`: the weak Nullstellensatz for an algebra of finite type, with
  points written as `k`-algebra homomorphisms `A → k`.
* `New.exists_mem_colon_of_tangent`: a criterion for an ideal to cut out a section of an affine
  scheme of finite type near a point. Tangent vectors at a `k`-valued point `o` along the fibre are
  the `V`-algebra maps to the dual numbers `k[ε]` that reduce to `o`.
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosedLocal.multivariate_hensel` is a several-variable Hensel lemma
  for systems `x i = p i (x)` whose coefficients lie in the maximal ideal. Over a local domain in
  which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root
  (`New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosedLocal`), it follows from the local structure of étale algebras:
  a standard étale algebra is given by a monic polynomial, whose residual root lifts.
modules.literature:
All results are known. `New.exists_le_weight_of_mem_vanishingIdeal_pow` is a form of the
Combinatorial Nullstellensatz with multiplicity, over any field. Each variable u has a positive
integer κ(u) and the weight 1/κ(u). In place of a grid it uses a set of at least ∏κ(u) points at
which each u^κ(u) agrees with a polynomial of lower weighted degree. A nonzero polynomial vanishing
to order d at all these points then has a monomial of weighted degree at least d. Source: Alon,
Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (1999); Ball–Serra, Punctured combinatorial Nullstellensätze (2009).

modules.title: Sums of residues at simple real poles
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file computes sums of residues of rational functions whose denominator has simple real roots.
Let `p = nodal univ x` be the monic polynomial with the distinct roots `x i`. The residue of `F / p`
at `x i` is `F (x i) / p' (x i)`. This file also determines the sign of `p' (x i)` when the roots
are ordered.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.sum_eval_div_eval_derivative_nodal` and
  `sum_eval_div_sub_mul_eval_derivative_nodal`: two sums of residues at simple poles.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.eval_derivative_nodal`: the derivative of `nodal univ x`, the monic
  polynomial with roots `x j`, at the root `x i` is the product of the `x i - x j` over `j ≠ i`.
modules.literature: The residue sums rest on Lagrange interpolation.

modules.title: Flat base change in functor cohomology, and the base change adjunction for algebras
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Cohomology here is H^n(N, Φ) = Ext^n(N, Φ) in the category of functors from C to abelian groups,
where Φ is a functor to S-modules. For a module M over an S-algebra T, the base change map
`New.Variety.baseChangeMap` goes from M ⊗_S H^n(N, Φ) to H^n(N, M ⊗_S Φ).
`New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange N` says that this map is bijective for all S, T, Φ, n and all M flat
over S. The file proves bijectivity for N = ℤ[h_A], with h_A the functor represented by A, by the
Yoneda lemma, shows that for flat M the maps admit dévissage in N, and transfers bijectivity along
bijective comparisons. It also shows that base change of algebras is left adjoint to restriction of
scalars, and that ring maps send powers of p to powers of p.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.HasBaseChange.baseChangeMap_bijective_freeAb_reprBy`: the base change map is
  bijective for N = ℤ[h_A], by the Yoneda lemma.
* `New.Variety.HasBaseChange.devissage`: for M flat it admits dévissage, being compatible with the
  long exact sequences of short exact sequences.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.IsBijective.baseChangeMap_bijective_iff`: along a bijective comparison
  from an N with flat base change, base change by a flat M on the target holds exactly when the
  comparison stays bijective after tensoring the coefficients with M.
* `New.Variety.algBaseChangeAdj`: for a k-algebra S, the functor A ↦ S ⊗_k A
  (`New.Variety.algBaseChange`) is left adjoint to restriction of scalars
  (`New.Variety.restrictAlg`).
* `New.Variety.pointMap_algBaseChange_unit_bijective`: the base change S ⊗_k B represents Hom(B, -)
  on S-algebras.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.moduleCoeff`: A functor F from C to k-modules, regarded as a functor to abelian
  groups, so that it can serve as the coefficients of cohomology.
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to Z[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.tensorWith`: For a module M over the S-algebra T, the functor X ↦ M ⊗_S X from
  S-modules to T-modules.
modules.literature:
The arguments are the usual ones: the Yoneda lemma, exactness of tensoring with a flat module, and
the tensor-hom adjunction.

modules.title: Integral power series over ℂ_p: jets, the chain rule and the exponential
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
A power series over `ℂ_[p]` is called integral if it comes, through `New.seriesToCp`, from a series
with coefficients in the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.mem_range_seriesToCp`: a series in one variable is integral iff all its coefficients have
  norm at most one.
* `New.pderiv_subst`: the chain rule for partial derivatives of a substitution of power series.
* `New.jet_subst_linearSeries`: for a linear substitution `M`, the jet `P(∂) (F ∘ M) (0)` is the jet
  of `F` along the polynomial `New.linSubst M P` obtained from `P` by the transposed substitution.
* `New.expSubst`: the exponential `exp a` of a power series `a` in several variables without
  constant term; it turns finite sums into products (`New.expSubst_add`, `New.expSubst_sum`).
* `New.padicValNat_factorial_mem_Icc`: `n / (p - 1) - v_p(n!)` lies in `[0, K]` for `n < p ^ K`.
* `New.rpow_le_norm_factorial`: the lower bound `p ^ (-n / (p - 1)) ≤ ‖n!‖` for the `p`-adic norm.

Notions from other files:
* `New.jet`: the bilinear pairing `P(∂)F(0)` of a polynomial `P` with a power series `F`, the sum
  over exponents `d` of `d!` times the product of the `d`-th coefficients of `P` and `F`.
* `New.linearSeries`: the linear form `∑ c_i z_i`, as a power series in the variables `z_i`.
* `New.linSubst`: for a matrix `M` over `R`, the `R`-algebra map of polynomial rings that sends
  `X_b` to `∑_t M_(t b) X_t`.
modules.literature:
Known results: the chain rule and the functional equation of the exponential for formal power
series, and Legendre's formula for the valuation of a factorial.

modules.title: Perfect algebras, étale algebras over perfect rings, and constant Laurent polynomials
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Fix a prime p (the class `ThePrime p`). An algebra is perfect when x ↦ x^p is bijective; for hp :
p = 0, `frobPow hp 1` is this map x ↦ x^p as a ring endomorphism, and O♭ denotes the tilt of the
ring of integers of ℂ_p. The file constructs perfections of quotients and perfected blow-up charts,
and it shows that étale algebras lift along surjections and are perfect over a perfect base in which
p = 0. It also proves that a Laurent polynomial that is a polynomial both in T and in T⁻¹ is
constant.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.perfectRing_monoidAlgebra`: O♭[G] is perfect when G is a module over the non-negative
  rationals.
* `New.Variety.PerfectAlg.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_widePushoutShape`,
  `New.Variety.perfectRing_tensor`: if p = 0 in S, perfect S-algebras are closed under wide
  pushouts, so, for perfect S, under tensor products.
* `New.Variety.exists_perfection_quotient`: the perfection of B/t, for p = 0 in the base.
* `New.Variety.exists_perfect_blowup_charts`: for f, g in a perfect algebra B over a perfect ring
  with p = 0, perfected charts B₁ (where g ∣ f) and B₂ (where f ∣ g) form an exact sequence
  B → B₁ × B₂ → B₀ → 0; the proof splits Laurent polynomials by
  `New.Variety.surjective_toLaurent_add_invert`.
* `New.Variety.exists_etale_lift`: an étale algebra over a quotient of C lifts to an étale algebra
  over C.
* `New.Variety.perfectRing_of_etale`: an étale algebra over a perfect ring in which p = 0 is
  perfect.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.tilt`: The functor from p-adic tests to commutative O^♭-algebras sending a
  test S to its tilt S^♭.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.PadicComparison.Descent.AlmostDescent` for sources.

modules.title: Relations, relative lengths and Fitting ideals for Selmer group estimates
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file gives linear algebra for the Selmer group estimates. Conditions on a function `c : Γ → Bⁿ`
are written as relations: finitely supported matrix-valued `f` on `Γ` acting by `c ↦ ∑ γ, f γ • c γ`
(`New.relEval`). Sizes are lengths of modules in `ℕ∞`, and `addVal` is the valuation of a discrete
valuation ring, normalised to be 1 at a uniformiser. The zeroth Fitting ideal of a quotient is
controlled as relations are added.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.obeying R B`: the functions with values in `Bⁿ` killed by all relations in `R`. For
  `New.cocycleRelations ρ` these are the cocycles (`New.mem_obeying_cocycleRelations`).
* `New.relLength S T`: the length of `S / (S ⊓ T)`, with its monotonicity and additivity rules.
* `New.length_obeying_relationsOn_le`: the relations `New.relationsOn Z` of a finitely generated `Z`
  cut out a module of length at most `rank Z * length B`.
* `New.length_ker_le_addVal_det`, `New.exists_matrix_addVal_det_le_length`: lengths compared with
  valuations of determinants.
* `New.Lift.relLength_le_of_relations`: if `p ^ t L ≤ L'` and any `m + 1` elements of `L` killed by
  `p` modulo `L'` have a combination in `L'` with some coefficient `1`, the length of `L` modulo
  `L'` is at most `t m`.
* `New.Selmer.fittingIdeal.exists_addVal_le_relLength`: if `p ≠ 0`, `R` is Noetherian and
  `Φ (p • v) ∈ N` for all `v`, then for a condition `V` on the linear forms modulo `p`, some `c` of
  valuation at most the length modulo `V` of the forms that vanish on `Φ⁻¹ N` multiplies the Fitting
  ideal of an enlargement `K` of `N` into that of `N`; here `K` contains `Φ v` for every `v` killed
  by all the forms that satisfy `V`.
modules.literature:
Three standard properties of Fitting ideals are proved in the cases that are used, for fixed
generators: base change (Stacks Project, Tag 07ZA), the product rule for an exact sequence, and the
bound by a length.

modules.title: A matrix of relations with small block determinant valuation
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Linear algebra over a discrete valuation ring O (written `DVR O`) with normalized valuation
v = `addVal O` and fraction field K. The valuation of a determinant of relations is bounded by the
length of a module of solutions, taken modulo an element p or in K/O.

* `New.Selmer.exists_rows_addVal_det_le`: let ψ : A → M_d(O) be onto, N an A-submodule of A^ι, p ≠ 0
  and b < v(p). If the vectors modulo p killed by ψ(N) lie in a module of length at most b, then
  some square matrix B with rows in N has v(det ψ(B)) ≤ b, with ψ(B) read as a block matrix.
* `New.Selmer.divQuot`: the map x ↦ x/p from O/p to K/O (`New.Selmer.DivisibleQuot`). For p ≠ 0 it
  is injective with image the p-torsion.
* `New.Selmer.exists_rows_addVal_det_le_of_divisible`: the same bound when the vectors with entries
  in K/O killed by ψ(N) lie in a module of length at most b. It follows from the form modulo p and
  is the form that Ribet's lemma uses.

The idea: as ψ is onto, any d linear forms in the span of the rows of the ψ(t), t ∈ N, are the rows
of one ψ(t). So a basis of this span, divided into groups of d forms, gives B. The length of the
solutions bounds the determinant of such a basis by the duality lemma
`New.exists_matrix_addVal_det_le_length` for lattices in O^n.
modules.literature: General linear algebra over a discrete valuation ring (elementary divisors).

modules.title: Integrality of exponentials, logarithms and roots of power series
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
The file first shows that, over an algebraically closed valued field, there is an integral point at
which finitely many given polynomials are at least as large as all their coefficients. It then
bounds the coefficients of power series built by exponentials, logarithms and roots over `ℂ_[p]`.
There `v` denotes the additive valuation with `v(p) = 1`, so that `‖c‖ = p ^ (-v(c))`, and `v(g)`
for a series `g` is the infimum of the valuations of its coefficients. `expSubst g` is `exp ℂ_[p]`
substituted at `g`, written `exp g`, and `logOf f` is `log ℂ_[p]`, the series of `log (1 + X)`,
substituted at `f - 1`, written `log f`. For `g(0) = 0` it proves that `exp g` is integral when
`v(g) ≥ 1 / (p - 1)`, gives a divisibility criterion for `exp g - 1`, and shows that `exp g` lies in
a ring `𝒪[[T]]` if its `m`-th power does, for `m` prime to `p`.

The imported notions used in the statements are these.

* `seriesToCp` is the inclusion of the series with integral coefficients into all series over
  `ℂ_[p]`. Its range consists of the series whose coefficients have norm at most `1`.
* `IsSeriesGenerator B T` says that `T = X + ⋯` and that `B` is the ring of all integral series in
  `T`, written `B = 𝒪[[T]]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_val_coeff_le_val_eval`: at one integral point, finitely many polynomials are at least
  as large as all their coefficients.
* `New.norm_coeff_expSubst_le_one`: `exp g` is integral if `g(0) = 0` and `v(g) ≥ 1 / (p - 1)`,
  degree by degree.
* `New.norm_coeff_expSubst_sub_one_le`, `New.IsSeriesGenerator.mem_of_expSubst_smul_eq`: for
  `v(c) ≥ 1 / (p - 1)` and `g(0) = 0`, the number `c` divides `exp g - 1` if it divides `g`, and,
  for `c ≠ 0` and in a ring `𝒪[[T]]`, `c` divides `g` if it divides `exp g - 1`.
* `New.IsSeriesGenerator.expSubst_mem_of_pow_mem`: if `g(0) = 0` and `(exp g) ^ m ∈ 𝒪[[T]]` with `m`
  prime to `p`, then `exp g ∈ 𝒪[[T]]`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the Gauss norm equals the supremum norm on the unit polydisc over an algebraically
closed valued field. Source: Bosch, Güntzer and Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*.

Known result: the integrality of the `p`-adic exponential and logarithm on series of large enough
valuation, and of the binomial series with exponent in `ℤ_p`.

modules.title: Maximal minors and lengths
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
Let `A` be a matrix over a discrete valuation ring `O` and let `a ≠ 0`. The length of the kernel of
`A` on `(O / a) ^ k` is the least valuation of a maximal minor of the matrix formed by the rows of
`A` and of `a • 1`. The kernel is isomorphic to the module of linear maps to `O / a` from the
quotient of `O ^ k` by these rows, so it has the length of this quotient, which is computed by the
Smith normal form and the multilinearity of the determinant.

* `New.Selmer.maximalMinors`, `New.Selmer.matrixKernel`: the minors and the kernel.
* `New.Selmer.isLeast_length_matrixKernel`: the statement for a matrix over a commutative ring `Λ`
  and a ring homomorphism `ev : Λ →+* O` with `ev a ≠ 0`.

Notions from other files:

* `New.QuotSpan a`: the quotient ring `O / a O`.
* `New.intGL k R`: the invertible matrices that, with their inverses, have entries in the subring
  `R`. The Smith normal form is stated for these, and here `R` is all of `O`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Length of a matrix kernel modulo `a` over a discrete valuation ring via maximal
minors. A consequence of the theorem on elementary divisors.

modules.title: Level moduli, residue data as Schwartz–Bruhat functions, and descent in positive degree
modules.group: Commutative algebra, cohomology and p-adic algebra
modules.note:
This file treats the modulus `M ^ c Q`, where `M` and `Q` are the products of two families of places
(the chosen places and the twist places) and `c` is a natural number. For a principal modulus
`(star g)` and a vector `x` with `g x` integral, it writes the translate of the vacuum by `x` as a
combination of the data `New.modDatum` of indicator functions of classes. Finally it proves a lemma
of algebra: if ∏ (T - a i) = 0 with all a i ≠ 0 and ∏ (S T^k - α i a i^k) = 0 for every k > 0, then
∏ (S - α i) = 0.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.places_levelModulus`: for `c ≠ 0` the places dividing `M ^ c Q` are the places of `M`
  and of `Q`.
* `New.isSchwartzBruhat_residueDatum`: the function `New.residueDatum w f` (`f` of the reductions
  at the places `w i` on matrices integral there, `0` elsewhere) is Schwartz–Bruhat
  (`New.IsSchwartzBruhat`) if no `w i` is conjugate to a `w j`.
* `New.Rows.liftFn_eq_residueDatum`, `New.exists_modulus_places_eq`: it is the lift of a function
  modulo a modulus `New.Modulus`, an ideal prime to its conjugate, with the same set of places;
  such a modulus exists if no `w i` is conjugate to a `w j`.
* `New.exists_rho_finVec_vacElem_eq_sum_modDatum`: if `𝔪 = (star g)` and `g x` is integral, the
  translate of the vacuum by `x` is a combination of the data `New.modDatum` of the indicator
  functions of classes modulo `𝔪`, with values of `New.stdLattice.selfDualAddChar` as coefficients.
* `New.GaloisRep.eval₂_prod_eq_zero_of_mul_pow`: the lemma of algebra just stated, for S and T in a
  ring that commute with the image of a ring homomorphism from a field K.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Modulus.liftFn`: A function Ψ of vectors mod 𝔪, read on finite adelic vectors: Ψ of the
  reduction if the vector is integral at the places of 𝔪 (`New.Modulus.places`), and 0 otherwise.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Weil.MixedModel.ZeroTerm` for sources.

modules.title: Orthogonality, Fourier inversion and matrix Gauss sums over a finite ring
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
Finite Fourier analysis on matrices over a finite commutative ring `R`, for a primitive additive
character `ψ` (no multiple `ψ (r * ·)` with `r ≠ 0` is trivial).

* `New.exists_primitive_residue_addChar`: a
  character of a ring `F` for which the subring `O` is self-dual induces a primitive character of a
  suitable quotient ring of `O`.
* `New.sum_addChar_dotProduct`, `New.sum_addChar_trace_mul`: orthogonality; the sum of `ψ` along
  a nonzero linear form on vectors or on matrices is `0`.
* `New.Exchange.matrixFourier`, `New.Exchange.matrixFourier_matrixFourier`: the transform
  `ρ ↦ ∑ v, f v * ψ (tr (ρ v))`, not normalised, and its inversion formula.
* `New.exists_sum_smul_addChar_trace_eq`: every function on matrices is a linear combination of
  the characters `y ↦ ψ (tr (y u))`.
* `New.Exchange.exists_matrixFourier_eq_mul_inv_det`: the transform of a function with
  `S (g d) = χ (det g) S d`, for a multiplicative character `χ` (zero off the units) that is
  primitive, `New.Exchange.IsPrimitiveMulChar`, and the modulus of the Gauss sum of `χ ∘ det`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Weil.TameGaussSum` for sources.

modules.title: Matrix norm estimates, the Ostrowski–Taussky inequality, and the complex Gaussian integral
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
This file proves estimates for complex matrices and computes the complex Gaussian integral on
`ι → ℂ`. Here `‖A‖` is the `ℓ²` operator norm. For accretive `A`, the integral of
`exp (-x* A (x - a))` against normalised Lebesgue measure is `(det A)⁻¹`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.norm_apply_le_l2_opNorm`, `New.l2_opNorm_le_of_apply`: the operator norm bounds the entries,
  and for an `m × n` matrix it is at most `|m| |n|` times a bound for the entries.
* `New.ostrowski_taussky`: the Ostrowski–Taussky inequality, in the form
  `|det H| ≤ 2 ^ card n |det Θ|` when `0 ≤ H ≤ Θ + Θᴴ`.
* `Matrix.IsAccretive`: the matrices `A` with `A + Aᴴ` positive definite. Positive definite matrices
  are accretive (`Matrix.PosDef.isAccretive`), and accretive matrices have nonzero determinant
  (`Matrix.IsAccretive.det_ne_zero`).
* `New.Fock.normalizedVolume`: Lebesgue measure divided by `π ^ card ι`, so that `exp (-|x|²)` has
  integral `1`.
* `New.Fock.map_mulVec_addHaar_eq_smul`, `New.lintegral_eq_norm_det_sq_mul_lintegral_mulVec`: the
  change of variables by an invertible complex matrix `u`, whose real Jacobian is `‖det u‖ ^ 2`.
* `New.Fock.integral_gauss`: if `A` is accretive, the integral of `exp (-x* A (x - a))` is
  `(det A)⁻¹`.
modules.literature: The Ostrowski–Taussky inequality and the complex Gaussian integral are known results.

modules.title: Fourier inversion for periodic functions and decay of Fourier transforms
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
This file develops Fourier analysis on a compact quotient `B ⧸ B₀` of a topological abelian group,
for a family of characters given in advance. `New.IsContPeriodic B₀ F` says that `F` is continuous
and `B₀`-periodic, and `New.quotMean B₀ F` is its mean over `B ⧸ B₀` for the Haar probability
measure.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsDualFamily`: a family `χ i` of characters of `B` trivial on `B₀`, multiplicative in the
  index, that separates the points of `B ⧸ B₀`.
* `New.IsDualFamily.tsum_coeff_eq_quotMean`: the mean of a series of characters with summable
  coefficients.
* `New.IsDualFamily.fourier_inversion`: Fourier inversion, from `New.stone_weierstrass_span`.
* `New.IsDualFamily.eq_zero_of_quotMean_mul_eq_zero`: a periodic function vanishes if its Fourier
  coefficients vanish at the characters that respect its quasi-periods (`New.RespectsQuasiPeriods`).
* `New.exists_pow_mul_norm_fourier_le`: for smooth `c` and `q`, with `c` supported in a compact set
  `K`, for `0 < ‖a‖ ≤ 1` and every `M`, the norm of the Fourier transform of `c · exp (q / a)` at
  `b` is at most a constant times the supremum over `K` of `‖exp (q / a)‖` divided by
  `(‖a‖ * (1 + ‖b‖)) ^ M`.
modules.literature:
The results of this file include the Stone–Weierstrass theorem for a monoid of functions, Fourier
inversion on a compact quotient of an abelian group, and the decay of Fourier transforms by
integration by parts.

modules.title: Strong operator integrals, analyticity of parameter integrals, and Hua's integral bound
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
In the strong integral, operator-valued functions are integrated vector by vector, so no
measurability in the operator norm is needed. In the results on analytic families, E is a
finite-dimensional complex normed space, K a compact R₁ space and f : E → K → ℂ a family of
functions on K with parameter in E. The file also contains the Schwarz lemma in normed spaces,
holomorphy of dominated parameter integrals, a uniqueness result for analytic functions along
submersions, and Euler's beta integral together with Hua's bound for negative powers of
determinants.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.strongIntegral`: the operator `x ↦ ∫ y, F y x ∂μ`, when this map is a bounded operator.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsAnalyticFamily`: the map x ↦ f(x, ·) into the Banach space C(K, ℂ) is
  analytic at a point.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsAnalyticFamily.analyticAt_integral`: then x ↦ ∫ f(x, k) dμ(k) is analytic,
  for a finite Borel measure μ.
* `New.analyticAt_of_eventually_differentiableAt`: a map between finite-dimensional complex spaces
  that is differentiable near p is analytic at p.
* `New.eventually_differentiableAt_integral`: an integral of holomorphic functions of a parameter in
  a finite-dimensional space, dominated by an integrable function, is holomorphic.
* `New.hua_integral_le`: Hua's bound for the integral of a negative power of `|det (M + Yᴴ Y)|`,
  where `Y = X S + A`, over the rows of `X`, one row at a time;
  `New.lintegral_norm_det_add_inv_pow_le` is a cruder form for `Y = S X + c` and at least seven
  columns.
modules.literature:
Known result: an upper bound for Hua's determinant integral. The integral is bounded only from
above, with an affine change of the rows, instead of being computed exactly. Source: Hua, Harmonic
Analysis of Functions of Several Complex Variables in the Classical Domains, AMS 1963.

modules.title: Packing bounds for separated points and Sobolev trace inequalities
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
The first results count and sum over points `f i` of a finite-dimensional real normed space `V` at
mutual distance at least `m > 0`. Here `d = finrank ℝ V`. The remaining results bound the value of a
function at a point by `L²` norms of the function and of its derivatives, first on an interval and
then at the corner of a cube.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.encard_le_of_separated`: at most `(1 + 2R/m)^d` such points lie in the ball `‖x‖ ≤ R`,
  where `R ≥ 0`, by comparing volumes.
* `New.tsum_le_of_separated`: if `u i ≥ 1`, `‖f i‖ ≤ R * u i`, `R ≥ 0`, `d < A` and
  `A ≤ c (A - d)`, then `∑ u i ^ (-A) ≤ (1 + 2R/m)^d * c`, by the layer bound
  `New.DiscreteSeries.integral_rpow_neg_le_of_measure_le`.
* `New.tsum_inv_pow_le_of_separated`: if the points satisfy `‖f i‖ ≥ m` and `n ≥ d + 2`, then
  `∑ ‖f i‖⁻¹ ^ n ≤ (5/m)^n`.
* `New.sobolev_trace`: if `‖g'‖ ≤ b` pointwise on `[0, ε]`, where `0 < ε ≤ 1`, then
  `‖g 0‖² ≤ ∫₀^ε (2/ε) (‖g‖² + b²)`.
* `New.sobolev_trace_cube`: its iteration over the coordinates of a cube `[0, ε] ^ D` and a
  parameter space, for functions `f i` indexed by the words `i` in a finite alphabet, where the
  norms of the partial derivatives of `f i` are bounded by `Λ ∑ l, ‖f (l :: i)‖`, the sum over the
  letters `l`.

modules.title: Circle means, Taylor series at zero, a power bound, and smooth matrix operations
modules.group: Real and complex analysis
modules.note:
This file proves mean value facts for circle averages and a halving criterion for upper bounds. It
develops the algebra of Taylor series at 0 of analytic functions and proves an elementary bound of
x^l by a factorial and exponentials. It also gives smoothness rules for matrix operations and
extends analytic germs to globally smooth maps.

The imported notion `New.taylorAtZero f` is the formal power series whose `n`-th coefficient is
`iteratedDeriv n f 0 / n !`, the Taylor series of `f : ℂ → ℂ` at 0.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.taylorAtZero_mul`, `New.taylorAtZero_comp_mul`, `New.eq_of_taylorAtZero_eq`: Taylor series
  at 0 of products and of `z ↦ f (a * z)`; such a series determines an entire function.
* `New.integral_eq_of_circle_mean`: an integral is unchanged when the integrand is replaced by its
  mean over a family of measure preserving maps indexed by the circle `ℝ / ℤ`.
* `New.integral_comp_toCircle_eq_apply_zero`: the mean value property over the unit circle of a
  function holomorphic on the closed unit disc, for the Haar probability measure of `ℝ / ℤ`.
* `New.le_of_halving`: let `c ≥ 0`. A function bounded above is at most `c` if each of its bounds
  can be halved at the points where it exceeds `c`.
* `New.exists_contDiff_eventuallyEq`: a map on a finite-dimensional space that is of class `C^ω`
  at a point agrees near it with a globally smooth map.
modules.literature:
The results of this file include the mean value property of holomorphic functions and the fact that
an entire function is determined by its Taylor series at 0.

modules.title: Line bundles on schemes via ring-valued points: descent and the Picard group
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
Line bundles on a scheme `X` are described through ring-valued points `t : Spec A ⟶ X`, so that
restriction maps disappear. A function `f : New.PointFn X` gives an element of `A` for every such
point. `New.LandsIn t U` says that `t` lands in the open `U`, and `f` is regular on `U` when it is
natural in `A` on the points of `U`. The file shows that regular functions come from sections and
that functions, sections and frames descend along flat, surjective, quasi-compact morphisms, and it
defines the Picard group with its pull-back.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.LineBundle`: a line bundle as an open cover with a cocycle of regular functions, with the
  operations `New.LineBundle.pull`, `New.LineBundle.one`, `New.LineBundle.inv`,
  `New.LineBundle.mul`.
* `New.LineBundle.IsSection`, `New.LineBundle.IsFrame`, `New.LineBundle.IsIsomorphic`,
  `New.LineBundle.H0`: sections, nowhere vanishing sections, isomorphism, and the module of
  sections.
* `New.PointFn.exists_ofSection_glue`: descent of functions along a flat, surjective, quasi-compact
  morphism.
* `New.LineBundle.exists_isSection_eq_mul`, `New.LineBundle.exists_isFrame_of_fpqc`: descent of
  sections and of frames along a flat, surjective, quasi-compact morphism.
* `New.Pic`, `New.LineBundle.picClass`, `New.Pic.pull`: the Picard group, written additively, the
  class of a line bundle, and the pull-back along a morphism.
* `New.Pic.eq_zero_of_isLocalRing`: the Picard group of the spectrum of a local ring is trivial.
modules.literature:
These are standard facts on line bundles and faithfully flat descent, in the language of ring-valued
points.

modules.title: Projective space, linear systems and projective embeddings, with Segre and Veronese
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
This file treats projective space `New.ProjSpace ι = Proj ℤ[X i]` and maps to it through ring-valued
points. A linear system (`New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`) is a line bundle given by a cover `U i`
and functions `g i j`. Each `g i j` is regular on all of `U i` and plays the part of `s j / s i`. A
projective embedding is a linear system `L` on `X` with a proper morphism `s : X ⟶ S`. In it, two
points of one chart with the same coordinates and the same image in `S` are equal. The file shows
that such embeddings determine morphisms and pass to closed subschemes and composites.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ProjSpace.hyperplaneBundle`, `New.ProjSpace.isLinearSystem_hyperplaneBundle`: the standard
  charts with `g i j = X j / X i` form a linear system.
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`: homogeneous coordinates of a point. Under a projective
  embedding, a point that lies in some chart is determined by its coordinates and its image in the
  base (`New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.eq_of_isHomogeneousCoords`). A vector with a unit entry is a
  vector of coordinates of some point of projective space
  (`New.ProjSpace.exists_isHomogeneousCoords`).
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding`, `New.isProjEmbedding_projSpace`: projective embeddings, by
  linear systems that separate points. Projective space over a base, with a finite index set, is
  one.
* `New.LineBundle.exists_picClass_eq_pull_hyperplane`,
  `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem.exists_hom_projSpace`: finite families of sections without common
  zero, and finite linear systems, come from maps to projective space.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.exists_isClosedImmersion`: for finite `ι`, an embedding is a
  closed immersion into ℙ^ι × S.
* `New.LineBundle.isProjEmbedding_pi` (Segre), `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding.pow` (Veronese): a
  proper scheme with finitely many jointly separating maps to embedded schemes embeds, and the
  `m`-th tensor power of a projective embedding is one for `m ≠ 0`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PointFn`: a function on ring-valued points of X attaches an element of A to every point Spec
  A → X, for every ring A, with no compatibility required. It is regular on an open U if its value
  at Spec φ ≫ t is φ of its value at t, for every t landing in U and every ring map φ.
* `New.LineBundle.IsSection`: the family (s_i) is a global section of L: each s_i is regular on U_i,
  and s_i = g_ij s_j at points landing in U_i and U_j.
* `New.LandsIn`: the morphism t : Y → X lands in the open U, that is, t⁻¹U is all of Y.
* `New.PointFn.ofSection`: a section s over U as a function on ring-valued points: its value at t :
  Spec A → X is t*s in A if t lands in U, and 0 otherwise.

modules.title: Dense families of complex points: reduced closures, separation of maps, and arcs
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
Identities between functions or morphisms on a reduced scheme can be checked on a dense family of
complex points. `New.IsDenseFamily ξ` says that the points `ξ z : Spec ℂ ⟶ X` have dense image, and
`New.IsSeparatingFamily ξ` says that moreover `X` is reduced. Every family of complex points factors
through its reduced closure, on which it is separating.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_reduced_closure`: any family of complex points of `X` factors through a closed
  subscheme in which it is `New.IsSeparatingFamily`, namely the reduced closure.
* `New.IsSeparatingFamily.pointFn_ext`, `New.IsSeparatingFamily.hom_ext`: regular functions, and
  morphisms over `S` to a scheme separated over `S`, that agree at the points are equal.
* `New.IsSeparatingFamily.exists_map_of_coords`: if a linear system on `X` gives the points `e z`
  the same coordinates as a projective embedding of `G` gives points `p z`, then it comes from a
  morphism `X ⟶ G` that sends `e z` to `p z`.
* `New.exists_valuative_arc_of_isDenseFamily` joins any point of a locally noetherian scheme with
  finitely many dense complex points to one of them by an arc `Spec V → S`, with `V` the ring of a
  valuation of `ℂ` in `ℝ≥0`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PointFn X`: rules that attach an element of `A` to every ring-valued point `Spec A ⟶ X`.
  It is regular on `U` (`IsRegularOn`) if, at points landing in `U`, it commutes with ring maps.
* `New.LineBundle X ι`: an open cover `U_i` of `X` with transition functions `g_ij`.
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`: `v` is a vector of homogeneous coordinates of the point `t`,
  that is, `t` lands in `U_j` exactly when `v_j` is a unit, and then `g_jk(t) = v_k / v_j`.
* `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem`: the data of a map to projective space, the model being
  `g_ij = s_j / s_i` on `U_i = {s_i ≠ 0}` for sections `s_i` without common zero.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding`: a linear system on a proper `X ⟶ S` for which points in one
  chart with the same affine coordinates and the same image in `S` are equal.

modules.title: Geometric points, specialisation, separating products and integral abelian varieties
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
Let `k` be an algebraically closed field. For schemes and morphisms locally of finite type, points
with values in `k` detect nonempty locally closed sets and images of morphisms, and this is used to
spread properties over commutative group schemes.
Smooth morphisms are shown to be geometrically reduced, and abelian schemes over `k` are shown to be
integral. The file also records that flat morphisms are injective on stalks. Finally it gives
criteria for families of complex points to be separating over a stalk of the base and on a product
of flat schemes.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_section_mem`, `New.exists_point_mem`: a nonempty locally closed set in a scheme
  locally of finite type over `k` contains a `k`-point.
* `New.IsDenseFamily.of_fibres`: if the complex points `η i` are dense in `S` and `A` is smooth over
  `S`, a family containing every complex point of `A` over the `η i` is dense in `A`.
* `New.AddObj.property_of_isOpenImmersion`: take a commutative group scheme (`New.AddObj`) locally
  of finite type over `k`. A property induced by a property of ring maps spreads from a nonempty
  open part to the whole scheme, by translation.
* `New.AddObj.smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_fibres`: the relative dimension of an abelian scheme can
  be read off the fibres through a dense family of points.
* `New.isSeparatingFamily_stalk`: for `A` and `S` reduced and dense points of `A` with finitely many
  images in `S`, the lifts of those that factor through a stalk of `S` separate the base change of
  `A` to that stalk.
* `New.IsSeparatingFamily.prod`: separating points of `B`, paired with dense points of the fibres of
  `A` over their images in `S`, separate `A ×_S B`, for `A`, `B` flat and locally of finite type,
  `A` reduced, and `S` reduced, locally noetherian, with finitely many dense complex points.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsDenseFamily`: the images of a family of complex points are dense.
* `New.IsSeparatingFamily`: the family is dense and the scheme is reduced.
* `New.IsAbelianScheme`: a smooth proper commutative group scheme on which multiplication by every
  `m ≠ 0` is surjective.
* `New.translation`: translation x ↦ x + z by a section z of a commutative group scheme.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Shimura.AbelianScheme.IsogenyFlatness` for sources.

modules.title: Functors of points on algebras: open subfunctors, étale charts, atlases, charted schemes
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
A space over `k` is a functor `X` from commutative `k`-algebras (`New.Variety.CommAlg k`) to types.
`New.Variety.reprBy A` is the functor represented by `A`, and `New.Variety.pointMap y` is the map
`reprBy A ⟶ X` given by a point `y ∈ X(A)`. The file defines open subfunctors and separated
functors. It also defines étale charts `a`, which are algebras `R` with étale coordinates and a
point `y ∈ X(R)` embedding `Spec R` as an open subfunctor `a.locus`. For `k` Noetherian it develops
the calculus of charts and shows that an atlas yields a cover by pieces étale over tori.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsOpenSubfunctor`, `New.Variety.IsSeparatedFunctor`: open subfunctors and separated
  functors, each defined by an ideal attached to one or two points. `New.Variety.IsAffinelyCovered`:
  separated, and covered by one affine after restriction along a functor `ι : C ⥤ CommAlg k`.
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart`, `New.Variety.IsChartCovered`, `New.Variety.HasAtlas`: affine open charts
  with étale coordinates, and covers of the field-valued points by charts.
* `New.Variety.etale_polyEval_iff`: for `k` Noetherian and `R` of finite type, coordinates are étale
  iff maps lift uniquely along square-zero extensions once the values of the coordinates are lifted.
* `New.Variety.HasAtlas.exists_isCharting`: an atlas gives a subfunctor satisfying
  `New.Variety.IsCharting`. It is found as a finite union of charts whose coordinates are units,
  that is, of pieces étale over a torus.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.isClosedClass`: for a comparison of cohomologies on categories over `D`,
  the functors on `D` for which it is bijective form a closed class
  (`New.Variety.IsClosedClass`: contains `0` and, given a short exact sequence whose first term is
  in it, contains the second term iff the third).
* `New.Variety.IsCharted`: a scheme is charted if its functor of points has a subfunctor satisfying
  `New.Variety.IsCharting`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsPointwiseSurjective p`: the map `p : E ⟶ Y` of functors is surjective on `A`-points
  for every object `A`.
* `New.Variety.IsZariskiLocallyTop`: every point maps into the given subfunctor once some element
  outside any given maximal ideal of the algebra is made a unit.
* `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.whisker`: for a subfunctor `U` of `Y` and `φ : C' ⥤ C`, the subfunctor
  `φ ⋙ U` of `φ ⋙ Y`.
* `New.Variety.restrictAlg k k'`: restriction of scalars, which regards a commutative `k'`-algebra
  as a `k`-algebra.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Cohomology.Etale.FilteredLimits` and `Lib.PadicComparison.ToricTower` for sources.

modules.title: Functors of points of proper schemes: closed loci, atlases and descent of relations
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
Schemes over `Spec R` are studied through their functors of points. The functor of points of a
proper scheme is proper and separated. On comparable rings (`New.Variety.IsComparableRing`), its
points all come from one affine scheme. If the scheme is smooth of relative dimension `d` after base
change to `k`, it also has an étale atlas.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.exists_ideal_le_ker_iff_factors`: for a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and a point `a`
  of `X` with values in `S`, one ideal `I` of `S` describes the ring maps `γ : S →+* B` along which
  `a` lands in `Z`, namely those that kill `I`. It is finitely generated if `i` is of finite
  presentation.
* `New.Variety.exists_locallyOfFiniteType_forall_factors`: a proper scheme `X` over `Spec R`
  receives a morphism `Spec T ⟶ X` from one affine scheme, locally of finite type, through which
  every point with values in a comparable ring (`New.Variety.IsComparableRing`) factors.
* `New.Variety.isProperOver_pointsToBase`: the functor of points of `X` over `R` satisfies
  `New.Variety.IsProperOver`.
* `New.Variety.isSeparatedFunctor_algPointsOf`: for an `R`-algebra `k` and a proper scheme `W` over
  `Spec R`, the points of `W` with values in `k`-algebras form a separated functor
  (`New.Variety.IsSeparatedFunctor`).
* `New.Variety.hasAtlas_algPointsOf`: if moreover `W` is smooth of relative dimension `d` after base
  change to `k`, the functor has an atlas of dimension `d`.
* `New.Variety.isAffinelyCovered_algPointsOf`: on rings satisfying `New.Variety.IsComparableRing`,
  one affine scheme surjects onto the points of a proper `W`.
* `New.Variety.exists_hom_of_rel` builds a homomorphism A → B of commutative group objects over S
  from a homomorphism f : W → B and a relation between T-points of W and of A. The relation is
  stable under pull-back and subtraction, compatible with f, and defined on an fpqc cover of A.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsComparableRing`, applied to the identity map of a ring: for any a, b in the ring
  there is an idempotent e with a ∣ e * b and b ∣ (1 - e) * a.
* `New.Variety.pointsToBase`: For a morphism s: X → Spec R, the map from the functor of points of X
  to the functor A ↦ Hom(R, A) that sends x ∈ X(A) to the ring map R → A of s∘x.
* `New.Variety.HasAtlas`: X is separated and has finitely many charts, each with exactly d étale
  coordinates, that contain every field-valued point.
* `New.Variety.IsOpenSubfunctor`: V is an open subfunctor of X: each x ∈ X(A) has an ideal I of A
  such that, for φ: A → B, φ(x) ∈ V(B) iff φ(I)B = B.
* `New.IsAdditive`: The morphism f : A → B of commutative group objects is a homomorphism: composing
  with f is additive on U-points for every U.
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.Cohomology.Etale.FilteredLimits` and `Lib.PadicComparison.HodgeTate.PeriodMap` for
sources.

modules.title: Absolute Frobenius, Serre's theorem on sections of powers, and projective embeddings
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
A line bundle (`New.LineBundle`) is an open cover `U i` with a cocycle `g i j`, and `L.picClass` is
its class in the additively written Picard group. `New.LineBundle.IsLinearSystem` says that the
transition functions behave like the affine coordinates `s j / s i` of a map to a projective space.
The file shows that the absolute `l ^ f`-Frobenius multiplies the class of a linear system by
`l ^ f`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.absFrobenius f X`: the absolute `l ^ f`-Frobenius of a scheme `X` over a field of
  characteristic `l`. It acts on `B`-valued points through `x ↦ x ^ l ^ f` on `B`
  (`New.Variety.comp_absFrobenius`), commutes with all morphisms and fixes the underlying space.
* `New.Variety.eventually_span_coordSection`: let `N` be a projective embedding of an integral
  scheme over a field and `p` a base change to a noetherian ring. For large `m` the monomials of
  degree `m` in the coordinates span the sections of `(p^* N) ^ m`.
* The instance `New.isProper_pi`: the product in `Over S` of a finite family of proper schemes over
  `S` is proper over `S`.
* `New.Variety.HasProjEmbedding.of_isClosedImmersion_pi`: if finitely many `S`-schemes have
  projective embeddings over `S`, so does every closed subscheme of their fibre product.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LineBundle.pull`, `New.LineBundle.pow`: the pull-back of a line bundle along a morphism, and
  its `m`-th tensor power, whose charts are indexed by `m`-tuples of indices.
* `New.LineBundle.IsProjEmbedding`: a linear system on a proper scheme whose affine coordinates
  `g i j` separate the ring-valued points of each chart `U i` over the base.
* `New.Variety.coordSection`: the `j`-th coordinate `s j` of a linear system as a global section.
* `New.ThetaTori.formSpan R x m`: the values at a family `x` of the forms of degree `m` over `R`.
modules.literature:
Known result: a case of the surjectivity half of Serre's theorem on sections of powers of a
projective embedding.

modules.title: Complex points over countable rings, Zariski generic members and Galois coverings
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
This file collects tools for passing between points of schemes over a countable ring and complex
points, and for building Galois coverings from complex points: extensions of embeddings of countable
rings into ℂ, an injective character of the algebraic closure of a finite field, Zariski generic
members of holomorphic families, reduced closures of families of complex points, and criteria for
coverings to be étale or smooth.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_ringEquiv_extend`: two embeddings of a countable ring, into `ℂ` and into an
  algebraically closed field of the same cardinality, are matched by an isomorphism of the fields
  (Steinitz's classification, relative to the ring).
* `New.exists_ringHom_complex_extend` lets one view a point over a field of cardinality at most that
  of ℂ as a complex point, compatibly with given embeddings of a countable base ring in the field
  and in ℂ.
* `New.Variety.exists_generic_member`: if `X` is locally of finite type over a countable ring and
  `φ` is a holomorphic family of complex points of `X` on a connected open set `U`, some `φ b`
  specialises, in the Zariski topology, to every `φ c`.
* `New.Variety.ReducedClosure`: the reduced closure in a finite product of schemes over `S` of a
  family of complex points; `New.Variety.ReducedClosure.exists_lift` constructs maps between two
  such closures.
* `New.Variety.isGaloisCovering_of_complex_points`: over a countable domain whose maps to fields of
  characteristic 0 are injective, a surjective map from a proper to a separated scheme, with a
  finite group acting simply transitively on its fibres of complex points, is a Galois covering.
* `New.Variety.IsGaloisCovering.smoothOfRelativeDimension_baseChange`: for a Galois covering
  `W → Z` over a domain `R`, with `W` proper and reduced and `Z` separated and smooth, the base
  change of `W` to a field of characteristic 0 containing `R` is smooth.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsGaloisCovering`: Δ is a finite group of automorphisms of W over c : W → Z, c is
  surjective, and Δ acts simply transitively on the fibres of c on points with values in fields of
  characteristic 0.
* `New.LandsIn t U`: the morphism t lands in the open U, that is, the preimage of U is everything.
* `New.HolomorphicAt φ w`: for every function regular on an open set containing φ w, the nearby
  members of the family φ land in that open set and the function pulls back to one analytic at w.
  The parameter space is a finite-dimensional complex normed space (`FinComplexSpace`).
* `New.IsSeparatingFamily ξ`: the scheme is reduced and the complex points ξ z are dense in it.
modules.literature:
The isomorphisms of fields come from Steinitz's theorem, and the étaleness criterion is that of
Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg.

modules.title: Smoothness near an arc from an immersive generic family and a bound on the tangent space
modules.group: Schemes through points, line bundles and charts
modules.note:
A criterion for smoothness of a scheme `X` over a normal domain `R` near an arc `Spec V ⟶ X`, where
`V` is a valuation subring of `ℂ`.

* `New.Variety.exists_landsIn_smoothOfRelativeDimension`: the criterion.

Idea: by the tangent bound, `d` functions map `X` to affine `d`-space over `R`, unramified at the
closed point of the arc. The holomorphic family makes this map dominant, so it is étale there.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LandsIn`: The morphism t: Y → X lands in the open U, that is, t⁻¹U is all of Y.
* `New.IsHolomorphicImmersionAt`: A family of complex points is holomorphic at a parameter and
  constant to first order only in the direction 0.
* `New.specMap`: The morphism of spectra given by a ring homomorphism.
* `New.Variety.sqZeroReduction`: The morphism from Spec R to Spec (R ⊕ M) given by the projection
  of the trivial square-zero extension.
* `New.PointFn.ofSection`: The function on ring-valued points given by a section s over U: its value
  at t is t*s if t lands in U, and 0 otherwise.

modules.title: Integral, congruence and unitary matrix groups over a ring, with their topology
modules.group: Matrix groups, characters and group algebras
modules.note:
The file opens with a few general facts on induction, reindexing, compact, open and closed sets, and
integrability.

* `New.intGL`, `New.congruenceGL`: the matrices of `GL n R` that are invertible over a subring `O`,
  and the congruence subgroups among them; `New.intGL.toMatrix` reads such a matrix over `O`, and
  `New.intGL.map` applies a ring map out of `O`.
* `New.U`: the unitary group of a matrix `J`, the `g` in `GL n R` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`, with change
  of ring `New.U.map`, change of basis `New.U.conj` and determinant `New.U.det`.
* `New.U.isClosedEmbedding_coe`: for invertible `J`, `U J` is closed in the space of matrices; with
  the bound on the entries of a unitary matrix, this gives that the complex unitary group of the
  identity matrix is compact.

The file also supplies the Polish and Borel instances on units, the measurable and measure space
structures on matrices, the Polish instance on unitary groups and the Borel instance on complex
ones, local compactness of unitary groups, and the additive Haar measure on matrices.

modules.title: The index of a product of subgroups is the product of the indices
modules.group: Matrix groups, characters and group algebras
modules.note:
One lemma of group theory, `New.Seesaw.index_pi_univ`: in a finite product of groups, the index of a
product of subgroups is the product of their indices (an infinite index is read as `0`).
modules.literature:
Known result: the index of a product of subgroups in a finite product of groups is the product of
the indices. Mathlib's `Subgroup.index_pi` is the case where all the factors are the same group.

modules.title: Block triangular groups, unipotent Bessel groups, Levi and parahoric subgroups
modules.group: Matrix groups, characters and group algebras
modules.note:
This file treats matrix groups over a commutative ring `R`, with an involution where unitary groups
are concerned. The space has the basis `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, then a middle block, then `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ`; the
index type is `New.SplitIndex ϱ μ`. The form `New.Shape.Form.splitGram T` consists of `ϱ` hyperbolic
planes and the middle Gram matrix `T`. In `New.Shape.BesselIndex` the middle block is `κ` and one
more vector `z`.

The file also defines the Kronecker product of a finite family of matrices and the character
`New.wave` of `ℂ`.

* `New.BesselIndex.level`, `New.Shape.besselFrame`, `New.Shape.Form.frameGram`: the levels of the
  basis vectors, the frame `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, and the products of the frame with its image under
  a matrix `γ`.
* `New.parabolic`, `New.agreeWithOneOn`, `New.unitriangular`: the block upper triangular matrices
  for a level function, the invertible matrices that agree with the identity on the entries picked
  out by a relation, and the block upper triangular matrices with all diagonal blocks `1`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselU0`: subgroups of the unitary group
  `New.Shape.Form.G` cut out by such conditions, where `New.U` is the unitary group of a Gram
  matrix.
* `New.levi`, `New.parahoric`: the Levi subgroups and the parahoric subgroups of `GL_k` over a
  commutative local ring.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.FloorGroups` for sources.

modules.title: ℚ/ℤ, characters of profinite groups, and extension of homomorphisms
modules.group: Matrix groups, characters and group algebras
modules.note:
`New.QZ` is `ℚ/ℤ` with the discrete topology, and a character of a profinite group `G`
(`New.QZChar G`) is a continuous homomorphism `G → ℚ/ℤ`. The file first proves elementary facts:
the exponential embedding of `ℚ/ℤ` into `ℂˣ`, the embedding of `ZMod n` into `ℚ/ℤ`, extension of
homomorphisms into divisible groups, and equality of the orders of a finite abelian group and its
dual. It then shows that characters separate points of the topological abelianisation of `G`, and
that additive maps from characters to `ℚ/ℤ` are evaluations at its points; these facts are used to
build Artin maps from their values on characters. `New.QZChar.abelianLift χ` denotes the map
induced by `χ` on the abelianisation, with values written multiplicatively.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.QZ.exists_extend`: for abelian groups, homomorphisms to a divisible group extend along any
  homomorphism whose kernel they kill.
* `New.card_hom_QZ`: a finite abelian group and its dual have the same order.
* `New.QZChar.mem_of_forall_abelianLift`, `New.QZChar.abelianization_ext`: characters separate a
  point from a closed subgroup of the abelianisation, and hence separate points.
* `New.QZChar.exists_hom_abelianLift_eq`: every additive map from characters to `ℚ/ℤ` is evaluation
  at a point of the abelianisation, in a form that is multiplicative in a parameter.
* `New.QZChar.continuous_iff_forall_isOpen_ker_comp`: a homomorphism from a commutative topological
  group to the abelianisation is continuous exactly when its composite with each character has open
  kernel.
* `New.exists_monoidHom_extend`, deduced from `New.QZ.exists_extend`: a homomorphism
  `θ` from a commutative group into a divisible commutative group, trivial on the preimage of a
  subgroup `H` under a homomorphism `f` of commutative groups, factors through `f` by a homomorphism
  trivial on `H`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Z1 ρ`: the continuous 1-cocycles of `ρ`, that is the continuous `f : G → M` with
  `f (g h) = f g + ρ g (f h)`; `New.QZChar G` is the case of the trivial action on `ℚ/ℤ`.
* `New.QZChar.toHom χ`: the character `χ` as a group homomorphism to `ℚ/ℤ` written
  multiplicatively; `New.QZChar.ker χ` is its kernel.

modules.title: Characters of finite groups: averages, virtual characters and central projections
modules.group: Matrix groups, characters and group algebras
modules.note:
This file sets up the character theory of a finite group `G` that is used for the characters of
`GL n` over a finite field. From Wedderburn's theorem it derives criteria for irreducibility.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsIrreducibleChar`: characters of norm one that satisfy the convolution identity with every
  class function.
* `New.virtualChars S G`: the `S`-span of the characters, a subalgebra of `G → ℂ`; for `S = ℤ` these
  are the virtual characters, for `S = ℕ` the characters (`New.isChar_of_mem_virtualChars`).
* `New.IsCentralProj`: central idempotents e of the group algebra ℂ[H] of any group H. Their
  coefficients are class functions; 1 − e, the image of e under a ring endomorphism of ℂ and tensor
  products are again central idempotents.
* `New.IsClassFunction.isIrreducibleChar_of_classInner_eq_intCast`,
  `New.IsClassFunction.mem_virtualChars`, `New.IsClassFunction.exists_eq_mul_groupAlgElem_mul`:
  criteria for a class function `f` to be an irreducible character, for `f` to be a combination of
  characters with coefficients in a given semiring, and for an element of `ℂ[G]` to be recovered
  from its product with `New.groupAlgElem f`. They are collected in
  `New.isIrreducibleChar_and_mem_virtualChars_and_exists_mul`.
* `New.IsCentralProj.isChar_card_mul_coeff`: for a central idempotent `e` of `ℂ[G]`, the function
  `g ↦ |G| · e(g)` is a character. Its pairing with any character is the rank of an idempotent, so a
  natural number. It is the character of a representation of dimension at most `|G|`
  (`New.IsCentralProj.exists_character_eq_and_finrank_le_card`), so the coefficients of `e` have
  norm at most `1` (`New.IsCentralProj.norm_coeff_le_one`).
* `New.IsCentralProj.self_adjoint`, `New.IsCentralProj.sum_norm_sq_conv_le`: a central idempotent of
  `ℂ[G]` acts self-adjointly for every `G`-invariant form that is sesquilinear for `σ⁻¹ ∘ conj ∘ σ`,
  complex conjugation transported along an automorphism `σ` of `ℂ`. So it acts as an orthogonal
  projection in every unitary representation. Hence convolution with it does not increase `ℓ²`
  norms.

modules.title: Chains of linear maps, tensor products of their data, and separation by forms
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
The file composes initial segments of a chain of linear maps and computes the index of the
stabiliser of a nonzero vector in a finite general linear group. It extends a chain of bilinear
steps from pure data to arbitrary tensors of the data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.index_stabilizer_GL_vector`: over a finite field `F`, the stabiliser in `GL n F` of a nonzero
  vector has index `|F| ^ |n| - 1`, by orbit-stabiliser.
* `New.TensorChain`: the tensor product `S (j-1) ⊗ (⋯ ⊗ (S 0 ⊗ ℂ))`, which is `ℂ` for `j = 0`.
* `New.TensorChain.lift`, `New.TensorChain.lift_pure`: for `x` in `M 0`, the linear map to `M j`
  that sends a pure tensor to the composite (`New.compUpTo`) of the maps `b i (f i)`, `i < j`,
  applied to `x`.
* `New.TensorChain.ofPairs`, `New.TensorChain.lift_ofPairs`: data of double steps regrouped into
  single factors.
* `New.tensor_eq_zero_of_separating`: over a principal ideal domain, if the forms `f i` on `U` have
  no common zero but `0` and `V` is torsion-free, then the maps `U ⊗ V → V`,
  `u ⊗ v ↦ f i u • v`, have no common zero but `0`.

modules.title: Eigenvalues: traces of powers, common eigenvectors, Amitsur's theorem, Sylvester's law
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file collects linear algebra on eigenvalues and characteristic polynomials. It expresses traces
of powers and determinants such as `det (1 - c N)` through the roots of the characteristic
polynomial.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_eigenvector_of_commute`: common eigenvectors of endomorphisms that preserve a
  finite-dimensional subspace `S` and commute on it, over an algebraically closed field.
* `New.exists_eigenvector_of_trace_mul_eq`: if twisted traces of a commuting family `A'` are
  proportional to traces of a commuting family `A`, a generalised eigensystem of `A` on which one
  operator has non-zero trace extends to an eigensystem of `A'` that is invariant under the twist.
* `New.amitsur_charpoly_mem_of_span` (Amitsur): for an algebra map to matrices, it suffices to check
  on a spanning set that the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials lie in the base ring.
  The proof works with det (1 - t ρ(w)) modulo a power of t and factors 1 - t ρ(w) step by step.
* `New.isConj_diagonal_of_isRoot_charpoly`: a complex square matrix whose characteristic polynomial
  vanishes at pairwise distinct numbers x_i, one for each index i, is conjugate to the diagonal
  matrix with entries x_i.
* `New.sylvester_law_of_inertia`: Sylvester's law of inertia for sign matrices.
modules.literature:
Known result: Amitsur's theorem that integral characteristic polynomials on a spanning set give them
on the whole algebra. It is a consequence of Amitsur's formula for the characteristic polynomial of
a sum of matrices. Source: S. A. Amitsur, On the characteristic polynomial of a sum of matrices,
Linear and Multilinear Algebra 8 (1980), no. 3, 177-182; G. Chenevier, The p-adic analytic space of
pseudocharacters of a profinite group and pseudorepresentations over arbitrary rings, LMS Lecture
Note Ser. 414 (2014), (1.5).

modules.title: Determinants of positive semidefinite matrices, principal minors and hermitian involutions
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
The file proves inequalities and identities for complex matrices. The norm of a matrix is the `L²`
operator norm, and `≤` between matrices is the positive semidefinite order. It also studies a
hermitian involution `J` and its unitary group `New.U J`, the group of invertible matrices `g` with
`gᴴ * J * g = J`, with real coordinates on skew-hermitian matrices. For signs `ε i = ±1`,
`New.signMatrix ε` is their diagonal matrix and `New.USign ε` its unitary group.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.norm_det_le_norm_det_of_posSemidef`: `0 ≤ P ≤ Q` implies `|det P| ≤ |det Q|`.
* `New.norm_det_sq_le_of_posSemidef`: if the block matrix with rows `(P, A)` and `(B, Q)` is
  positive semidefinite, then `|det A|² ≤ |det P| |det Q|`.
* `New.principalMinor`: the principal minor on the indices satisfying a predicate `p`.
* `New.jacobi_complementary_minor`: Jacobi's theorem, the principal minors of `x⁻¹` from the
  complementary principal minors of `x`.
* `New.IsHermitianInvolution J`: `J` is hermitian and `J * J = 1`. Examples are `1` and the diagonal
  matrices of signs `New.signMatrix ε`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Haar.TotalMass` for sources.

modules.title: Integral matrices over subrings: Smith normal form, Gelfand's condition and lattices
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file studies matrices over a commutative ring `A` that are integral with respect to a subring
`R`. The model is the ring of integral adeles inside the finite adeles. `New.IsIntMatrix R M` says
that all entries of `M` lie in `R`. The property `New.IsValuationPair R` says that of two elements
of `A` one divides the other over `R`, piece by piece along an idempotent of `R`. The file also
defines column lattices and indices of lattices, and studies principal congruence subgroups of
unitary groups.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsValuationPair.smith_normal_form`: a square matrix over `A` is diagonalized by row and
  column operations over a subring `R` that satisfies `New.IsValuationPair`.
* `New.exists_invTransposeGL_inv_eq`: for such a subring `O` of `R`, `gᵀ` lies in the double coset
  `GL n O * g * GL n O`.
* `New.IsHeckeFunction.heckeFun_adjoint`, `New.IsHeckeFunction.heckeFun_comm`: adjoints and
  commutativity of Hecke operators for `K = GL n O`, with `O` a valuation subring of a field.
* `New.submoduleIndex`, `New.denomIndex`: the relative index of two `R`-modules, and the index of
  the denominator of `a`. An infinite index is read as `0`.
* `New.colLattice`, `New.preimageLattice`: the span of the columns of `M`, and the vectors `M` makes
  integral.
* `New.unitaryLevel`: the principal congruence subgroup of the unitary group `New.U J`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.intGL n O`: for a subring `O` of `R`, the subgroup of `GL n R` of matrices that have,
  together with their inverse, all entries in `O`.
* `New.U J`: the unitary group of `J`, the `g` in `GL n R` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`.
* `New.heckeFun π K f`: the operator `∑ f g • π g`, summed over chosen representatives `g` of
  `G ⧸ K` (zero if infinitely many terms are nonzero).
* `New.IsHeckeFunction K f`: `f` is left and right `K`-invariant and supported on finitely many
  cosets `g K`.
* `New.levelSpace π K`: the vectors of the representation `π` that are fixed by `K`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n. This file proves the case that
is used, by Gelfand's trick: over a valuation subring of a field the Hecke operators commute on
fixed vectors of a representation. Source: J. Tits, Reductive groups over local fields, Corvallis
1979, 3.3.3; T. Tamagawa, On the zeta functions of a division algebra, Ann. Math. 77 (1963).

Part of a known result: the valuation pairs and integral matrices of this file are groundwork for
Witt's extension theorem for unimodular hermitian lattices and for the Iwasawa decomposition (see
`Lib.Adelic.Witt.IwasawaDecomposition`).

modules.title: Matrices near the identity: Jacobi's formula and norm estimates
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file collects known facts on complex matrices near the identity.
It proves Jacobi's formula for the derivative of the determinant at the identity and
`det (exp M) = exp (tr M)`.
Estimates in the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, which is the norm of all matrices in this file, control the
inverse and the logarithm of `1 + X` and the exponential of `X`.
The logarithm of an element of `USign ε` near `1` lies in the Lie algebra.
A matrix at distance less than `1` from the identity is accretive.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.hasDerivAt_det_of_eq_one`: along a differentiable curve of complex matrices through the
  identity, the derivative of the determinant there is the trace of the velocity.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.logOneAdd` and `exp_logOneAdd`: the logarithm of `1 + X` for `‖X‖ ≤ 1 / 2`.

Notions from other files:
* `signMatrix ε` is the diagonal matrix with entries `ε i = ±1`, and `USign ε` is its unitary group.
* `unitaryLie J` is the space of matrices `X` with `Xᴴ * J + J * X = 0`.
* `entryMask r X` keeps the entries `(i, j)` of `X` with `r i j` and replaces the others by `0`.
* A matrix `A` is accretive (`A.IsAccretive`) if `A + Aᴴ` is positive definite.

modules.title: Products of principal minors, Fischer's inequality and the Cauchy–Binet formula
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
For an integer vector `w` and an invertible complex matrix `x`, m_w(x) = `New.weightMinors w x` is
the product over all integers `t` of the principal minors `New.principalMinor` of `x` on
`{i | t ≤ w i}`. The factors with `t ≤ 0` are divided by `x.det`. The file develops the calculus of
m_w and the closure properties of the invertible triangular matrices `New.IsBorelMatrix o`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.weightMinors_eq_det_zpow_mul_prod`: the finite form `x.det ^ a * ∏_{a < t ≤ b}` of minors,
  when `a ≤ w ≤ b`.
* `New.fischer_det_inequality`: for a positive semidefinite matrix in 2×2 block form,
  |det z| ≤ |det z₁₁| · |det z₂₂|.
* `New.fischer_inequality`: for positive semidefinite z, the principal minor
  (`New.principalMinor`) on a disjoint union of two index sets is at most, in absolute value, the
  product of the two principal minors.
* `New.hadamard_det_inequality`: for positive semidefinite z, |det z| is at most the product of
  the |z_ii|.
* `New.det_mul_eq_sum_minors`: the Cauchy–Binet formula.
* `New.det_fromCols_eq_sum_minors`, `New.sum_norm_det_fromCols_sq_le`: the Laplace expansion along
  a block of columns and a bound for its complementary minors.

modules.title: Gram determinants
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
* `New.exists_extend_basis_of_span_eq_top`: an independent family is completed to a basis by members
