  of a spanning set.
* `New.det_gram_comp`: `det ⟨u x_i, u x_k⟩ = (normDet u)² det ⟨x_i, x_k⟩` for a family `x` of as
  many vectors as the dimension of the source of `u`; here `(normDet u)² = det (u* u)`.
* `New.norm_det_mul_det_gram_mul_det_le_one`: a bound on a Gram determinant times `conj (det u')`
  and `det u` in a nonarchimedean field when the inner products of the families transformed by `u'`
  and `u` have norm at most `1`.
* `New.formGram`, `New.norm_det_formGram_le`, `New.norm_det_pairing_sq_le`: Gram matrices for a
  form given by a matrix; a consequence of Hadamard's inequality and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
  for determinants, for a positive semidefinite form.

Notions from other files:

* `Matrix.gram ℂ x`: the matrix of the inner products `⟨x_i, x_k⟩`.

modules.title: Minors, polynomials of matrices and twisted norms
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file contains general lemmas on matrices over commutative rings, and three definitions used
elsewhere: a minor of a matrix of variables, a non-degeneracy condition on a trace form and a
freeness condition on a family of integers.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.variableMinor_ne_zero`: a minor of a matrix of variables with distinct rows and distinct
  columns is not zero.
* `New.IsTraceNondeg r`: the trace form is non-degenerate on the span of the matrices `r g`.
* `New.HasNoSmallRelations e`: here `e : Fin n → ℤ`, with `n` a natural number. A sum of at most
  `(n + 1) ^ 2` of the integers `e i`, together with the number of terms, determines how often each
  `e i` occurs.
* `New.det_eval_eq_zero_iff_not_linearIndependent`: over a field, finitely many functions
  `v j : X → k` are linearly dependent if and only if all the determinants `det (v j (x i))` vanish.
* `New.charpoly_dvd_charpoly_aeval_comp`, `New.isUnit_aeval_iff_isCoprime`: the characteristic
  polynomial of `Y` divides that of `q(Y)` composed with `q`, and `z(Y)` is invertible iff `z` is
  coprime to the characteristic polynomial of `Y`.
* `New.exists_gl_map_eq_of_fixed`: an invertible matrix fixed by `σ` lifts along any injective
  ring map whose image contains the fixed points of `σ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.twistedNorm τ p δ`: the product `δ · τ(δ) ⋯ τ^(p-1)(δ)` in a monoid `M`, for `τ : M → M`.

modules.title: The unipotent radical attached to an idempotent matrix
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
For an idempotent matrix `ε`, the matrices `1 + ε Y (1 - ε)` form the unipotent radical of the
parabolic subgroup that keeps the image of `ε`. If a polynomial in `g` is a projection onto the
image of `ε`, then every translate of `g` by the radical is conjugate to `g` under the radical
(`semiconjBy_radicalHom_aeval_sub`).

modules.title: Hermite forms over valuation pairs and integral matrices over valued fields
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
We reduce the columns and rows of matrices over a ring `A` by invertible matrices over a subring
`R`, under the hypothesis `New.IsValuationPair`. It says that any two elements `a, b` of `A` are
`R`-multiples of `a - e * (a - b)` for some idempotent `e` of `R`. It holds for a valuation domain
`A` with `R = ⊤`. For a field with a valuation into `ℤᵐ⁰`, we bound the entries of matrix products
and give a determinant test for integral invertible matrices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsValuationPair.hermite`: Hermite form `y = U_ι * D` with `U ∈ GL_n(R)`, `D` block
  triangular.
* `New.IsValuationPair.exists_isPrimitiveMatrix_mul`: a matrix with a left inverse becomes primitive
  (`New.IsPrimitiveMatrix`) after multiplication by an invertible block triangular matrix.
* `New.IsValuationPair.exists_mul_clear_cols`: the transposed form, clearing the columns outside
  the image of `ι`.
* `New.mem_intGL_iff_det`: `g` lies in `New.intGL n 𝒪[F]` (the image of `GL n 𝒪[F]` in `GL n F`) iff
  its entries are integral and `v (det g) = 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.intGL n R`: the subgroup `GL_n(R)` of `GL_n(A)` of matrices that have their entries and
  those of their inverse in the subring `R`.
* `New.transvectionGL`: for distinct indices `i, j` and `a` in `A`, the element `1 + aE_{ij}` of
  `GL_n(A)`, with inverse `1 − aE_{ij}`.
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix R X`: `X` has entries in `R` and a left inverse with entries in `R`.
modules.literature:
The property `New.IsValuationPair` and the Smith normal form are in
`Lib.General.LinearAlgebra.IntegralLattices`.

modules.title: Auerbach's lemma, ultrametric matrix bounds and Gram norms
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file collects norm estimates for linear maps and matrices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_auerbach`: linear forms indexed by a compact space that vanish together only at `0`,
  with images in a normed field depending continuously on the index, contain the coordinate forms
  of a basis on whose vectors all forms of the family take values of image norm at most `1`. These
  forms are chosen to maximise the norm of the image of their determinant; Cramer's rule gives the
  bound.
* `New.norm_mulVec_le_of_nonneg`, `New.norm_mulVec_le`: over an ultrametric field, a matrix whose
  entries have norm at most `c ≥ 0` multiplies the sup norm of a vector by at most `c`, whatever its
  size.
* `New.sqrt_weylNormSq_le_of_dual`: a bound on the Gram norm of Weyl modules by duality.
* `New.sqrt_weylNormSq_sum_le`: the triangle inequality for the Gram norm of Weyl modules.
modules.literature: Known result: Auerbach's lemma, here for a compact family of linear forms.

modules.title: Rows and columns of integral matrices, primitive matrices and the law of partners
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file develops linear algebra over a subring `O` of a commutative ring `R`, for the local
computations with partner functions. The index set `n` is split by `e : b ⊕ a ≃ n`. For
`k ∈ GL n R`, `New.firstCols e k` is the matrix of the columns `b` of `k`, and
`New.invLastRows e k`, `New.invFirstRows e k` are the matrices of the rows `a` and `b` of `k⁻¹`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.AreMatched`: two functions `Φ`, `Ψ` supported on the blocks `New.invLastRows e k` and
  `New.firstCols e k` of `k ∈ GL n O`, whose values differ by the factor `χ (det k)`.
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix.mul_iff`: for primitive `y`, the matrix `y * x` is primitive exactly if `x`
  is primitive.
* `New.exists_firstCols_eq_mul`: multiplying `firstCols e k` by an element of `GL b O` and
  `invLastRows e k` by an element of `GL a O` gives the blocks of another element of `GL n O`,
  whose determinant is computed.
* `New.IsValuationPair.exists_firstCols_iff`: if `New.IsValuationPair O` holds, the primitive
  matrices are the `firstCols e k` with `k` in `GL n O`.
* `New.AreMatched.lift_of_reduction`: partners over `R` lift along a surjective local homomorphism
  `O → R`; here `O` is a subring of another ring `F`.
* `New.AreMatched.left_mul`, `New.AreMatched.right_mul`: the transformation laws of two partner
  functions.

Notions from other files:
* `New.intGL n O`: the group `GL n O` as a subgroup of `GL n R`.
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix O y`: the matrix `y` and some left inverse of it have entries in `O`.
* `New.HasLeftInv X`: the matrix `X` has a left inverse over `R`.
* `New.liftIntegralFn π f`: the function that is `f` at the image under `π` of a matrix over `O`
  and zero at every other matrix.
* `New.IsValuationPair O`: for all `u`, `v` in `R` there is an idempotent `ε` in `O` such that `u`
  and `v` are `O`-multiples of `(1 - ε) u + ε v`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.SiegelWeil.Tower.LargeSideConstantTerm` for sources.

modules.title: Gram–Schmidt, tight frames, polar decomposition in U(p,q), forms representing one
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
This file collects four topics of linear algebra. The first is a Gram–Schmidt process
whose change of basis is block triangular for a weight on the columns. The second concerns tight
frames of `ℂ^Φ` made of vectors of the lattice `𝔞₀` attached to a CM field. The third is the polar
decomposition in the unitary group of a diagonal sign form, with properties of accretive matrices.
The last gives a condition under which a Hermitian form takes the value `1` on a subspace.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_orthonormal_mul`: the columns of a complex matrix with a left inverse
  (`New.HasLeftInv`) become orthonormal after right multiplication by an invertible matrix `b` that
  is block triangular for a given weight `wt` on the columns: `b i j = 0` whenever `wt j < wt i`.
* `New.IsTightFrame`: vectors of `𝔞₀`, with multiplicities, that form a tight frame of `ℂ^Φ`.
* `New.exists_polar`: `g = k * z` with `k` unitary and `z` positive definite and an exponential.
* `New.isAccretive_blockDiagPart_inv_mul`: the block diagonal part of `g` is invertible and
  `(blockDiagPart ε g)⁻¹ * g` is accretive.
* `New.exists_mem_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_one`: a Hermitian form on `ℂ^m` that is not negative
  semidefinite on a subspace takes the value `1` on that subspace.

Notions from other files:
* `New.signMatrix ε`: the diagonal matrix of the signs `ε`; `New.USign ε` is its unitary group, the
  invertible complex matrices `g` with `gᴴ * signMatrix ε * g = signMatrix ε`.
* `New.unitaryLie J`: the Lie algebra of this group for `J = signMatrix ε`: the real vector space
  of complex matrices `X` with `Xᴴ * J + J * X = 0`; `New.expU X` is `exp X` in the group.
* `Matrix.IsAccretive z`: the matrix `z + zᴴ` is positive definite.
* `New.WeilData E`: data on a CM field `E`; only its finite idele `α` is used here.

modules.title: Extending columns, block matrices and block embeddings
modules.group: Linear algebra and matrix analysis
modules.note:
For an embedding `ι : r ↪ n` of index sets, `New.inclMatrix k ι` has the standard basis vectors
`e (ι j)` as columns. Such a map splits `n` into two blocks, and the file studies the corresponding
block matrices. Over a field, independent columns extend to an invertible matrix. The embedding
`a ↦ diag(a, 1)` of unitary groups of sign matrices is a proper map, and the norm of a block
diagonal matrix is the larger of those of its blocks, for the L² operator norm.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.extendGL`: the embedding g ↦ diag(g, 1); `New.submatrix_extendGL` and
  `New.extendGL_apply_of_notMem_range` give its block g and its rows outside that block.
* `New.rangeParabolic`, `New.mem_rangeParabolic_iff`: the opposite parabolic for the two blocks, and
  its description in entries.
* `New.index_rangeParabolic_mul_card_GL`, `New.index_stabilizer_inclMatrix`: the index of the
  opposite parabolic times |GL_r(R)| is the index of the group that fixes the basis vectors of
  the first block, and over a finite field the latter index is computed.
* `New.residueDatum`: a function of adelic matrices given by their reductions at a family of
  places.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.isProperMap_inl`: the embedding `a ↦ diag(a, 1)` is a proper map.

Notions from other files:
* `New.parabolic`: the subgroup of GL_n(R) of matrices that are block upper triangular for a given
  level function on the indices.
* `New.U`, `New.U.sum`: U(J) is the group of g with gᴴJg = J; for a block diagonal sum J'' of J
  and J', `New.U.sum` is the homomorphism U(J) × U(J') → U(J'') sending (g,h) to diag(g,h).

modules.title: Measures below a fibre measure
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
Let `π : X → B` be a map, `μ` a measure on `X` and `ν` a measure on `B`. For a submersion of
manifolds with smooth positive measures, the fibre measures `dμ / dν` on the fibres of `π` are
determined by two properties: integrating over the fibres and then against `ν` is integrating
against `μ`, and the fibre integrals of a continuous function of compact support are continuous on
`B`. This file does not construct them. It defines the relation of being at most the fibre measure
over a point and proves that it is kept by the usual operations on measures and maps.

* `New.LeFibreMeasure`: a measure `l` is at most the fibre measure over a point `b`.
* `New.LeFibreMeasure.of_coordinates`: a parametrisation `ψ t p` of a part of `X` with
  `π (ψ t p) = t` and a weight `w t p`, both continuous at `t = b` and dominated by `μ`, give such a
  measure.
* `New.LeFibreMeasure.trans`: the relation for a pair of maps follows from the relations for the two
  steps, the second map being continuous.
* `New.LeFibreMeasure.map_prod`: the relation is kept by a family of maps that respect `π`.
modules.literature: Fibre measures: Weil, Sur la formule de Siegel dans la théorie des groupes classiques, no. 6.

modules.title: Fubini and convolution lemmas; idempotent kernels
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
General lemmas of measure and integration, and the notion of an idempotent kernel on a group.

* `New.IsBoundedMeasurable`: a strongly measurable function whose norm is bounded by a constant.
* `MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.integral_integral_comp`: Fubini's theorem along a
  measure-preserving map from a product; `MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.fubini` adds the
  integrability on the product.
* `New.integrable_integral_skew_product`, `New.integral_integral_skew_product`: Fubini's theorem
  after a substitution that preserves the measure on the space where it acts;
  `New.integral_skew_product` is the conjunction of the two.
* `New.integral_smul_integral_swap`, `New.integral_smul_integral_eq_integral_conv_smul`: the
  integral `∫ x, k x • ∫ g, α g • F (j x * g)`, for `g` in a group, in the opposite order and as a
  pairing with a convolution; `New.integral_conv` is the conjunction of the two.
* `New.IsIdempotentKernel`: a continuous integrable function `e` on a group with
  `e g⁻¹ = conj (e g)`, `e 1 ≠ 0` and `∫ e z * e ((z * x)⁻¹ * y) dz = e x⁻¹ / e 1 * e y`; in
  particular `e * e = e` (`New.IsIdempotentKernel.convolution_self`).
modules.literature:
The results of this file are standard. The lemmas on iterated integrals and on convolution on a
group are forms of Fubini's theorem, and `New.sq_lintegral_le` is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for
lower integrals, deduced from Hölder's inequality.

modules.title: Uniqueness of Haar measure, integrals over subgroups and Gaussian normalisation of volumes
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
The file treats three topics of measure theory. Two additive Haar measures on a locally compact,
second countable group agree if some real function has integral 1 for both. Integrals over compact
or open subgroups are computed by translation invariance, orthogonality of characters and reduction
to finite sums. A normalisation of volumes by Gaussian integrals is defined. It holds for `ℝ` and
`ℂ` and passes to binary products and finite powers under σ-finiteness assumptions.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.addHaar_eq_of_integral_eq_one`: uniqueness of additive Haar measure, with the constant fixed
  by the integral of one test function.
* `New.setIntegral_char`: orthogonality for a multiplicative function over an open subgroup.
* `New.setIntegral_eq_finsum`: over a compact `M`, a function constant on the cosets of an open
  subgroup `L` integrates to `ν (L ∩ M)` times a finite sum over `M ⧸ (L ∩ M)`.
* `New.HasGaussianIntegral`: the Gaussian normalisation of a volume.
* `New.HasGaussianIntegral.pi`: the normalisation on a finite power.
* `New.lintegral_inv_add_rpow`: the integral of `(c + q x) ^ (-s)`, computed through the Gamma
  function.

modules.title: Product measures, layer cake bounds, cocompact subgroups and L² bounds of integral operators
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
This file rearranges the coordinates of finite powers of a σ-finite measure space, bounds integrals
of negative powers under polynomial volume growth by a layer cake argument, shows that continuous
functions on a group G that are left invariant under a cocompact subgroup Γ are integrable for
finite measures on G, and passes L² bounds of integral operators with measurable, integrable kernels
to finite products. It also contains Tonelli's theorem for finite products, products of cocompact
subgroups, and two small constructions, `New.padTuple` and `New.unitOrOne`.

Among the imported notions in the statements are `Subgroup.FixesLeft Γ F`, meaning `F (γ g) = F g`
for `γ ∈ Γ`, and the following.

* `Subgroup.IsCocompact Γ`: some compact set `C ⊆ G` meets every orbit `Γg`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.lintegral_rpow_neg_le_of_measure_sublevel_le`: if the sublevel sets `{u ≤ R}` of a measurable
  function `u ≥ 1` have measure at most `(K R^e)^d V`, with `K ≥ 0`, then the integral of `u^(-A)`
  has an explicit bound for `A > e d`. The measure is arbitrary, so the result also bounds sums
  (counting measure). For finite `V`, `New.integrable_rpow_neg_of_measure_sublevel_le` and
  `New.integral_rpow_neg_le_of_measure_sublevel_le` are the forms for the Bochner integral;
  `New.DiscreteSeries.integral_rpow_neg_le_of_measure_le` joins them.
* `New.integrable_of_isCocompact`: continuous left Γ-invariant functions are integrable for finite
  measures on G.
* `New.IsL2Contraction`: a finite family of kernels defines an operator of norm at most one between
  two `L²` spaces, tested on bounded measurable functions. By `New.IsL2Contraction.pi`, the bound
  passes to the product of finitely many such families, for σ-finite measures and measurable kernels
  that are integrable in the last variable.

modules.title: Pushforward of Haar measures, the modulus of GL_n and the generalised index
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
This file compares Haar measures under pushforward and computes the factors by which maps scale
them. Mathlib's `distribHaarChar A g` is the factor by which `g` scales Haar measure on the additive
group `A`. For a unit `a`, `New.genIndex a` is the inverse of this factor for multiplication by `a`.
For a pair `R ⊆ A` with `New.IsAdelic R`, the indices of column lattices are expressed through
`genIndex` of determinants.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.measure_smul_map_restrict_eq_smul_inv`: the pushforward under a homomorphism of a
  bi-invariant measure restricted to a set `O`, compared with a left invariant measure on the
  target. The condition on `O` is `New.HasStableLifts`.
* `New.inv_distribHaarChar_eq_relIndex_div`: the inverse of the scaling factor is a ratio of
  relative indices of compact open subgroups.
* `New.genIndex`: the generalised index of `a : R`, for a unit the inverse of the factor by which
  `a` scales Haar measure on `R`, and `0` otherwise. Let `O` be a compact open subring and `a ∈ O`
  a unit of `R`. Then it is the cardinality of `O / a O` (`New.genIndex_eq_card`).
* `New.inv_distribHaarChar_GL_eq_genIndex_det`: `g : GL n R` scales Haar measure on `n → R` as
  `det g` does on `R`, if `R` has a compact open subring with the property `New.IsValuationPair`.
* `New.submoduleIndex_colLattice_div`: the ratio of the two indices between the column lattice of
  an invertible matrix and the standard lattice is `genIndex` of the determinant.
* `New.submoduleIndex_colLattice_intVectors`: if the matrix has entries in `R`, the index of its
  column lattice in the standard lattice is `genIndex` of the determinant.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsValuationPair O`: any two elements `a`, `b` of the ambient ring are `O`-multiples of
  `(1 - e) a + e b` for some idempotent `e` of the subring `O`.
* `New.IsAdelic R`: the subring `R` of `A` is open, compact, stable under `star` and satisfies
  `New.IsValuationPair`, with further properties that are not used here.

modules.title: Measures on hermitian quadrics: existence and uniqueness of disintegrations
modules.group: Measure theory, Haar measures and integration
modules.note:
This file develops measure theory on hermitian quadrics over a "place" `A`. The result is a measure
that is written `Dirac(h(x, x) - Γ) dx` and is determined by the disintegration property. Quadrics
and disintegrations are indexed by skew elements `b`, with `Γ = δ⁻¹ * b` for a skew unit δ.

* `New.Floors.Place`: the data and properties of a place. Here `skewMeasure`, written ν, is a Haar
  measure on the skew elements, and `skewUnit`, written δ, is a skew unit. For hermitian Γ, the
  element δΓ is skew (`New.Floors.Place.skewUnitMul`).
* `New.Floors.Place.flatChart`, `New.Floors.Place.quadricMeasure`: for hermitian `T`, an explicit
  chart of `h(x, x) = δ⁻¹ * b`, and the image of the flat measure under it. Here `h` is a hyperbolic
  plane plus `T` (`New.Floors.planeSumGram`).
* `New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration`: disintegrations along `h(x, x)`. For hermitian `T`, the chart
  measures form a disintegration of the volume (`New.Floors.Place.isDisintegration_quadricMeasure`).
  Disintegrations are unique at every skew `b` (`New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration.unique`). They
  move along a matrix `M` with `Mᴴ * J * M = T` that has a left inverse
  (`New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration.map`).

Notation: for a ring with involution, `skewAdjoint A` is the group of elements with `star x = -x`,
and `x⁻¹ʳ` is the ring inverse, which is zero at non-units. The vector `x ⊕ᵥ y` on a disjoint union
of index sets is `x` on the first part and `y` on the second. The group `U T` consists of the
invertible matrices g with `gᴴ * T * g = T`.

modules.title: Frobenius orbits of roots over finite fields and residue fields at self-conjugate places
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
This file collects arithmetic lemmas on finite fields and on finite places of a CM field `E`. For
`P` irreducible over a finite field with `q` elements and a root `x` of `P` in an extension `K`, the
roots of `P` in `K` are the Frobenius conjugates `x^(q^i)`, `i < deg P`. For a CM field `E` with a
primitive root of unity of order `5040`, a place fixed by conjugation has a norm that is a square,
so places of prime norm are split. The file also contains two summation lemmas.

* `New.FinPlace E`: the finite places `w` of `E`, that is, the nonzero primes of `𝓞 E`; `star w` is
  the complex conjugate of `w`.
* `w.q`: the norm of `w`, that is, the number of elements of its residue field.
* `w.IsSplit`: the statement `star w ≠ w`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.card_selfAdjoint`: the size of a finite field with an involution that moves `√-1`.
* `New.two_notMem_of_star_eq`: if `E` contains an integer of trace `1` and even norm over its
  maximal real subfield, a place with `star w = w` does not lie above `2`;
  `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040.isSplit_of_two_mem` is the case of the hypothesis
  `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`.
* `New.exists_sq_eq_q_of_star_eq`: if moreover `E` contains `√-1`, such a place has norm
  `w.q = r ^ 2` with `r % 4 = 3`; `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040.exists_sq_eq_q_of_inert` is the case
  of the hypothesis `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`.
* `New.finite_prime_q_star_eq`, `New.isSplit_of_q_prime`: all but finitely many places of prime norm
  are moved by the conjugation, and all of them under the hypothesis `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`.
* `New.root_pow_card_pow_eq_self_iff`, `New.root_pow_card_pow_eq_iff_modEq`: `x^(q^n) = x` iff
  `deg P ∣ n`, and `x^(q^a) = x^(q^b)` iff `a ≡ b` modulo `deg P`.
* `New.aroots_eq_frobenius_orbit`, `New.aroots_pow_eq_frobenius_orbit`: with multiplicity, the roots
  of `P` in `K` are the `x^(q^i)` for `i < deg P`, and the roots of `P^j` are the `x^(q^i)` for
  `i < deg (P^j)`.
modules.literature: Known: standard facts on finite fields and on residue fields of CM fields.

modules.title: Embeddings, differents and the maximal real subfield of a CM field
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
The file collects general lemmas on differents and root discriminants of number fields. It then
compares a CM field `E` with its maximal real subfield E⁺ (`maximalRealSubfield E`), covering the
trace, the norm, the different and the discriminant.

* `star` is complex conjugation on the CM field `E` and on its integers `𝓞 E`.
* `Φ v` is the complex embedding chosen at the infinite place `v`: by `New.PlaceEmbedding` in
  general, and by `New.CMType`, which extends it, for CM fields.
* `New.volÔ E` is `2 ^ r₂ / √|disc E|`, with `r₂` the number of complex places of `E`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.differentIdeal_eq_span_of_dvd`: a criterion for `f'(x)` to generate the different and for
  `𝓞 L = A[x]`.
* `New.mem_maximalRealSubfield_iff_star_eq`, `New.trace_maximalRealSubfield_eq_add_star`,
  `New.norm_maximalRealSubfield_eq_mul_star`: E⁺ is the fixed field of conjugation, and the trace
  and norm from `E` to E⁺ are `x + x̄` and `x x̄`.
* `New.differentIdeal_eq_top`, `New.abs_discr_eq_discr_maximalRealSubfield_sq`: under
  `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040` the relative different is trivial and |disc E| = (disc E⁺)².
* `New.volÔ_eq`: the mass `New.volÔ` of the integral finite adeles in terms of the root
  discriminant.
* `New.exists_mixedEquiv_maximalRealSubfield`: the Minkowski space of E⁺ as real functions on the
  infinite places of `E`.
* `New.Variety.prod_embeddings_eq_prod_pairs`: a product over the complex embeddings of a totally
  complex field, grouped into conjugate pairs.

modules.title: The imaginary quadratic field ℚ(√−d): characters, Frobenius and splitting of primes
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
This file studies the imaginary quadratic field `K = ℚ(√-d)` (`New.QuadField`) for `d ≡ 3 mod 4`,
realised inside `ℂ`, and the Dirichlet characters attached to it. Throughout, `New.chiK d p` is the
Legendre symbol `(p / d)` of `p` modulo the prime `d`, and `New.QuadField.betaK d` is the algebraic
integer `(1 + √-d) / 2`. A finite place of `K` (`New.FinPlace`) is a nonzero prime of its ring of
integers. Below, `w` is a finite place that contains the rational prime `p`, and `w.q` is its
absolute norm. For a prime `d ≡ 7 mod 8` the file determines the ring of integers and the different
of `K`. For `d ≡ 3 mod 4` it shows how a rational prime `p` decomposes in `K`. It also proves two
consequences of lifting the exponent at `2` for integers, which do not involve `K`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.chiK`, `New.quadTwist`: the Legendre symbol `(·/d)` as an integer-valued character, and its
  product with a complex character `χ` modulo `N`, a character modulo `N * d`.
* `New.QuadField`: the field. For `d ≡ 3` modulo `4` it is a quadratic CM field
  (the degree is `New.QuadField.finrank_eq_two`). For a prime `d ≡ 3` modulo `4` it embeds in any
  field of characteristic zero with a primitive `d`-th root of unity
  (`New.QuadField.embOfPrimitiveRoot`).
* `New.QuadField.different_eq_span_and_adjoin_betaK`: for a prime `d ≡ 7` modulo `8`, the integers
  of `K` are `ℤ[(1 + √-d) / 2]` and the different is `(√-d)`.
* `New.FinPlace.q_eq_pow_inertiaDeg`, `New.FinPlace.inertiaDeg_dvd_iff_forall_pow_eq`: the norm of
  `w` is `p ^ f` with `f` the residue degree, and `f` is the order of Frobenius;
  `New.FinPlace.exists_q_eq_pow` states both together.
* `New.QuadField.q_eq_iff_chiK_ne_neg_one`: for `d` a prime `≡ 7 mod 8`
  (`New.PrimeSevenModEight`), `w` has degree one iff the Legendre symbol `(p / d)` is not `-1`.
* `New.QuadField.span_eq_or_exists_span_eq_mul`: `p` is inert in `K`, or it is the product of two
  places of degree one; `New.QuadField.prime_inert_or_eq_mul` also lists the places above `p`.

modules.title: Principal ideal powers, S-units and a class number bound
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
For every ideal `I` of a ring of integers of a number field some power `I ^ n` with `n ≠ 0` is
principal. For ideals of norm greater than 1 the generators can be chosen large at every complex
embedding.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaTori.exists_pow_eq_span_inv_lt`: for an ideal of norm greater than 1, some power is
  principal with a non-unit generator of arbitrarily large absolute value at every complex
  embedding.
* `New.SUnit.dirichlet_unit_theorem`: for a finite set `S` of finite places of a number field `K`,
  the `S`-units are finitely generated of rank `#S + #(infinite places) - 1`. This follows from
  Mathlib's unit theorem and the finiteness of the class number, in the form
  `New.exists_valuation_eq_exp_mul`. Valuations are multiplicative, with values in `ℤᵐ⁰`, and a
  uniformiser has valuation `exp (-1)`.
* `New.eq_zero_of_forall_norm_lt_one`: an algebraic integer of absolute value below `1` at every
  infinite place is `0`. Here `Φ v`, from an instance of `New.PlaceEmbedding`, is a chosen complex
  embedding that induces the infinite place `v`.
* `New.classNumber_le`: a number field of degree `n` and discriminant `d` has class number at most
  `(2 ^ n * |d|) ^ (n + 1)`.

Minkowski's bound is at most `2 ^ n * |d|` (`New.minkowski_bound_le_two_pow_mul_discr`), so each
class has an integral ideal of norm `k ≤ 2 ^ n * |d|` as a member. Such an ideal is generated by
`k` and one more element, and the proof counts the possible pairs.

* `New.conj_mem_quadInt`: for a prime `d ≡ 7` mod `8`, the ring `New.quadInt d`, the image of the
  ring of integers of ℚ(√−d) in ℂ, is stable under complex conjugation.
modules.literature:
Dirichlet's `S`-unit theorem is deduced from the unit theorem in Mathlib, and the class number bound
is a crude explicit form of the finiteness of the class number, deduced from Minkowski's bound in
Mathlib.

modules.title: Criteria for CM fields
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
This file gives two ways to show that a number field is CM. The first asks that the field contain a
totally complex field, and that complex conjugation be induced, in all embeddings at once, by a map
of the field to itself. The second shows that adjoining to a CM field a root of a suitable
polynomial gives a CM field, whose finite adeles it also describes.

We write `𝔸f K` for the ring of finite adeles of a number field `K`. For an extension `L / K` of
number fields, `𝔸f L` is an algebra over `𝔸f K`, and complex conjugation `star` of a CM field
extends to its finite adeles.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.isCMField_of_forall_exists_conj`: a number field is CM if it contains a totally complex field
  and complex conjugation is induced, in all embeddings at once, by a map of the field to itself.
* `New.isCMField_adjoinRoot_of_forall_root_mul_star_eq`: let `E` be a CM field and `P` an
  irreducible polynomial over `E`. If all complex roots of `P` have the same rational square
  absolute value `ν`, then `L = E[X]/(P)` is again CM.
* `New.aeval_root_finAdele_surjective`, `New.aeval_root_finAdele_eq_zero_iff`: for monic `P`, the
  finite adeles `𝔸f L` are obtained from `𝔸f E` by adjoining a root of `P`.
* `New.IsFinAdelePresentation`: a map from polynomials over `𝔸f E` presents `𝔸f L` as the quotient
  by `P`, compatibly with `E[X] → L` and with complex conjugation.
* `New.adjoinRoot_cm_presentation`: these facts about `L` and `𝔸f L` in one statement.

modules.title: Coefficient rings of ℓ-adic lattices, and length versus cardinality of modules
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
The coefficient rings over which ℓ-adic lattices are taken, and, for modules over an ℓ-adic
integer ring, a comparison of length with cardinality.

* `New.card_eq_pow_length`: over an ℓ-adic integer ring R with residue field k, a module of finite
  length has #k ^ length elements.
* `New.length_le_of_card_le`, `New.length_le_of_card_dvd`: an inequality of cardinalities (the
  smaller module being finite) or a divisibility of cardinalities gives an inequality of lengths.
* `New.CoeffRing ℓ`: the rings of integers O of finite Galois extensions of ℚ_ℓ inside ℚ̄_ℓ. Each is
  a finite ℤ_ℓ-module, compact, and a discrete valuation ring with divisibility read from the norm
  (`New.CoeffRing.dvd_iff_norm_le`).
* `New.CoeffRing.eventually_mem`: an element of norm at most 1 lies in all sufficiently large
  coefficient rings. That the rings are directed by inclusion is an instance.

Three imported notions occur in the statements:

* `New.ThePrime ℓ`: the class saying that ℓ is prime, which fixes the prime ℓ in scope;
* `New.DVR O`: O is an integral domain and a discrete valuation ring;
* `New.PadicIntegerRing R ℓ`: R is a discrete valuation ring of characteristic 0, finite and free
  over ℤ_ℓ, with finite quotients by nonzero ideals.

modules.title: Lattice indices, primitive matrices, Jacobi's identity and covolumes of fundamental domains
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
The first part is lattice algebra over an adelic pair `R ⊆ A` (`New.IsAdelic`; among its conditions,
`R` is open and compact in `A`), modelled on `New.Ô` inside the finite adeles. The file proves
results on indices and determinants under integral base change. For a CM field `E`, it then gives
tools for computing, coordinate by coordinate, the covolume of an arithmetic subgroup of a unipotent
group.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.genIndex_det_conj_of_isIntMatrix`: the size of a determinant does not change under an
  integral base change with integral inverse.
* `New.exists_isPrimitiveMatrix_mul_fromBlocks`, `New.exists_preimageLattice_eq_colLattice`: a left
  invertible matrix becomes primitive after multiplication by an invertible (block triangular)
  matrix.
* `New.exists_mulVec_eq_of_orthogonal`: for `J` hermitian and invertible, if the left invertible `F`
  and `n` have orthogonal columns, as many in all as `J` has rows, the orthogonal complement of `n`
  lies in the span of `F`.
* `New.genIndex_det_orthogonal_mul_submoduleIndex_sq`: Jacobi's identity between a lattice and its
  orthogonal complement; `New.Filling.jacobi_perp_discriminant` joins it with the previous result.
* `New.exists_fundamental_domain_classLattice`: the covolume of a lattice in `(E ⊗ ℝ)ⁿ` cut out by a
  finite adelic matrix and rescaled at the infinite places.
* `New.Filling.existsUnique_mul_mem_box`: suppose a group `Γ` shifts the coordinates of `G` in a
  triangular way by additive submonoids. Then the box over strict fundamental domains of these
  submonoids meets each coset `xΓ` exactly once.
* `New.Filling.exists_fundamental_domain_im_skew`: the covolume of the group
  `New.Filling.imSkewLattice` of rescaled purely imaginary integers of `E`, if `E` contains a
  primitive 5040th root of unity.

Notions from other files:
* `New.genIndex`: on units the inverse of the factor by which multiplication scales Haar measure,
  and `0` elsewhere; `New.submoduleIndex M M'`: the index of `M ∩ M'` in `M'`, as additive groups
  (`0` if infinite).
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix`: a matrix with entries in `R` and a left inverse with entries in `R`.
* `New.colLattice`: the `R`-module spanned by the columns of `M`; `New.preimageLattice`: the
  `R`-module of vectors `v` over `A` such that `M v` has entries in `R`.
* `New.Variety.classLattice g S Q`: the image, under the CM embedding followed by the linear map
  `Q`, of the group of `y` in `Eⁿ` such that the class of `g⁻¹ y` in `(𝔸_f/Ô)ⁿ` lies in `S`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.Adeles.Basic` and `New.Spanning.RemainingTerms.SiegelLemma` for sources.

modules.title: Algebraicity from ℓ-adic bounds, roots of unity as limits, and the ℓ-adic valuation
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
This file proves three groups of facts. `New.isAlgebraic_of_norm_complexToCp_le` shows that a
complex number that stays ℓ-adically bounded under all isomorphisms ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ, for one prime ℓ, is
algebraic. The second section approximates the roots of unity ζ in ℂ_p with ζ^{q_p} = ζ by images of
integers of K = ℚ(√−d); the third collects properties of the ℓ-adic valuation and of coefficient
rings.

* `quadInt d` is the ring of integers of K inside ℂ, and a `PadicPlace p` fixes a map ιₚ : ℂ → ℂ_p.
* `primeNorm d p` is the number q_p, equal to p² if the Legendre symbol `chiK d p` = (p/d) is −1 and
  to p otherwise.
* v = `New.ellVal` is the normalised valuation on ℚ̄_ℓ = `PadicAlgCl ℓ`, truncated to 0 on elements
  of norm at least 1, so that its values lie in [0, ∞].
* O denotes a ring in `New.CoeffRing ℓ`: the ring of integers of a finite Galois extension of ℚ_ℓ
  inside ℚ̄_ℓ. `ThePrime ℓ` says that ℓ is prime.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.mem_normPairClosure_of_pow_eq`: an element `ζ` of `ℂ_p` of norm 1 with `ζ ^ q_p = ζ` is a
  limit of images of integers `α` of `K`, in such a way that the image of `α ᾱ` tends to
  `ζ ^ (p + 1)`.
* `New.CoeffRing.normLength`, `New.CoeffRing.normLength_addVal`: the rescaling of lengths of
  O-modules that sends the additive valuation of x to v(x), so that they become comparable for
  different O.
* `New.CoeffRing.eventually_exists_isPrimitiveRoot`: all large O hold a primitive k-th root of
  unity.
modules.literature:
Known result: Teichmüller representatives as limits of powers. Source: Serre, Local Fields, Chapter
II.

modules.title: The Gauss valuation of a polynomial over the ring of integers of ℚ̄_ℓ
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
The function `New.ellVal` agrees with the valuation `v` only on integral elements of `ℚ̄_ℓ`, so
almost everything is stated over their ring `ℤ̄_ℓ`. The first sections collect the rules of `v`
there and show that monic polynomials split, that every nonnegative rational number is the valuation
of some element, and that the residue field is algebraically closed. For a rational number `ρ ≥ 0`,
called the radius, and `g = ∑ y_i Y ^ i` put `v_ρ(g) = min_i (v(y_i) + ρ i)`.

* `New.Selmer.gaussVal`, `New.Selmer.gaussVal_le_eval`: `v(g(y)) ≥ v_ρ(g)` if `v(y) ≥ ρ`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_forall_ellVal_eval_eq_gaussVal`: for finitely many polynomials equality holds
  at one such point.
* `New.Selmer.gaussVal_mul`, `New.Selmer.gaussVal_eq_add_sum_roots`: `v_ρ` is additive on products,
  and it is given by `v₀(g)` and the valuations of the integral roots.
* `New.Selmer.exists_one_add_pow_eq`: a solution of `(1 + x') ^ j = 1 + x` of large valuation.
* `New.Selmer.le_ellVal_geom_sum`, `New.Selmer.ellVal_pow_sub_one_le`: bounds for the valuations of
  geometric sums of elements near `1` and of `ζ ^ j - 1` for roots of unity `ζ` of `ℓ`-power order.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v` on `ℚ̄_ℓ` with `v ℓ = 1`, cut off below at `0`; `New.intQpBar ℓ`
  is the ring `ℤ̄_ℓ` of integral elements, and `x.1` is `x` as an element of `ℚ̄_ℓ`.
* `New.ThePrime ℓ`: `ℓ` is prime.
modules.literature:
Known result: Gauss norms and Gauss's lemma for polynomials over the integral elements of ℚ̄_ℓ.
Source: Bosch, Güntzer, Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis.

modules.title: Coefficient rings with a large residue field
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
Adjoining the roots of unity of order `ℓ ^ k - 1` to a finite extension of `ℚ_ℓ` multiplies the
degree by at most `k` and gives a residue field with at least `ℓ ^ k - 1` elements. The extension is
unramified, but this is not needed: the ramification index is at most the degree, which grows
linearly in `k`, while `ℓ ^ k` grows faster.

* `New.Selmer.frequently_lt_card_residueField`: beyond every coefficient ring there is one whose
  residue field is large compared with the ramification index.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CoeffRing ℓ`: rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`, ordered
  by inclusion;
* `New.ThePrime ℓ`: the class saying that `ℓ` is prime.

modules.title: Coefficient rings inside the ring of all integral elements
modules.group: Number fields, local fields, adeles and lattices
modules.note:
Elementary facts on the inclusion of a coefficient ring into `ℤ̄_ℓ`, and a divisibility statement
for geometric sums in a ring with a divisibility-reflecting map to `ℤ̄_ℓ`.

* `New.CoeffRing.toIntQpBar`: the inclusion, which reflects divisibility
  (`New.CoeffRing.dvd_of_toIntQpBar_dvd`).
* `New.Selmer.pow_dvd_geom_sum`: for `α` near `1`, a high power of `ℓ` divides `∑ i < ℓ ^ N, α ^ i`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CoeffRing`: rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`;
  `New.CoeffRing.normLength` rescales `ℕ∞`-valued lengths over such a ring, a uniformiser `ϖ` having
  length `v(ϖ)`, so that lengths over different rings are comparable.
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v` on `ℚ̄_ℓ` with `v ℓ = 1`, cut off below at `0`; `New.intQpBar ℓ`
  is the ring `ℤ̄_ℓ` of integral elements; throughout, the instance `ThePrime ℓ` fixes `ℓ` as the
  prime in play.
